PLAYER RATINGS | Augsburg 3-1 Mainz – Michael Gregoritsch ends Augsburg’s winless streak

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1416 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Getfootballnewsgermany

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Bundesliga battle between two teams desperate to snap poor runs of form ended in favor of the Bavarian Swabian hosts.
  • The hosts entered Sunday’s encounter hovering just above the relegation zone, three places below Urs Fischer’s Mainz.
  • According to recent reports, baum, already dealing with a banged-up defensive corps, had to contend with more bad news this week in the form of injuries to central defenders Chrislain Matsima and Jeffrey Gouweleeuw.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Bundesliga battle between two teams desperate to snap poor runs of form ended in favor of the Bavarian Swabian hosts. Two matchdays into the current Bundesliga campaign, Manuel Baum’s Augsburg were celebrating their status as the top team in the table. Unfortunately, Baum’s Fuggerstädter then proceeded to go seven league fixtures without a win. That streak is now history following a 3-1 home win over Mainz.

The hosts entered Sunday’s encounter hovering just above the relegation zone, three places below Urs Fischer’s Mainz. Fischer’s team nevertheless only possessed one point more and counted as one of the biggest disappointments of the German top flight. The Rheinhessen traveled to Bavaria on a four-match losing streak, including a loss to 2. Bundesliga outfit Bochum that dumped them out of the Pokal in the second round.

According to recent reports, baum, already dealing with a banged-up defensive corps, had to contend with more bad news this week in the form of injuries to central defenders Chrislain Matsima and Jeffrey Gouweleeuw. Matsima’s absence forced the FCA trainer to hand 18-year-old prospect Tim Schnitzer his Bundesliga starting XI debut. Captain Gouweleeuw, meanwhile, could luckily enough be replaced by Manchester City loanee Juma Bah, who had returned from suspension. Schnitzer and Bah were among five changes to the starting XI Baum employed in the recent 5-2 away defeat to RB Leipzig. Marius Wolf, Michael Gregoritsch, and Alexis Claude-Maurice started over Han-Noah Massengo, Arijon Ibrahimovic, and Rodrigo Ribeiro.

Sources indicate that fischer too needed to pull the trigger on several changes. Though the Mainz trainer declared himself largely satisfied with the performance of his team in a narrow loss against Bayern Munich just prior to the international break, four new outfielders took to the pitch for the Rheinhessen. Fischer, having several of his preferred starters back, sent Phillip Tietz, Phillipp Mwene, Paul Nebel, and Stefan Posch onto the field in place of Ransford Königsdörffer, Silvan Widmer, Jae-Sung Lee, and Fabio Gruber. Posch returned from suspension after getting sent off in a disastrous encounter against Elversberg that saw Fischer’s charges dispatched 4-1.

Recent findings suggest that baum’s changes certainly produced attractive football in the opening stages. Wolf’s placement as the right wingback enabled the reliably versatile Robin Fellhauer to slide inside and work in the packed midfield alongside Fabian Rieder, Claude-Maurice, and Anton Kade. This particular FCA foursome strode forward with reckless abandon, mostly keeping Mainz pinned back in their own half throughout the entire first quarter-of-an-hour. Sharp combos involving the midfield and the wingbacks produced plenty of incursions into the FSV penalty area. Kade unfortunately couldn’t find the right angle on the best of the opportunities to score, shooting well wide from only six meters out in the 12th minute.

The opener finally came on Augsburg’s second corner of the afternoon. A quality free-kick from Claude-Maurice was actually shepherded out into touch deftly by former FCA striker Phillip Tietz in the 19th minute. Newly minted FCA record holder Gregoritsch was able to convert the subsequent set-piece for the 1-0. Makeshift Augsburg defender Yannik Keitel did an excellent job beating Mainz’s Kaishu Sano in an aerial duel after Rieder swung in the corner from the right. Keitel’s header was initially saved by Robin Zentner, who parried the ball toward the far post. The rebound fell perfectly for the onrushing Gregoritsch, who easily slid in his sixth Bundesliga goal of the campaign. As Baum and his crew knew full well, however, an early lead meant little.

It has been revealed that in their ongoing seven-game winless run, Augsburg had actually squandered the lead in six of them. On five occasions, Baum’s team scored the opening goal of the match. Some five minutes after Gregoritsch opened the scoring, it appeared as if another lead was almost certain to evaporate. Somehow, one of Mainz’s most dependable scorers spurned a chance to equalize. Tietz found himself free in front of goal in the 24th off a blitz counter, but blasted the ball well over the bar in front of his former FanKurve. Apart from that chance, the Bavarian Swabian hosts did still remain the more active side.

The 2-0 finally came off yet another corner from the right in the 36th minute. This time, fellow fresh starter Bah would bundle home another Rieder corner when Mainz couldn’t get the service from the right clear. Amid all the jostling prior to Bah bundling the ball home, the second goal withstood VAR scrutiny. Regrettably, the rest of the half would fall prey to officiating controversies. A sequence of events shortly after the second goal promptly led to match official Martin Petersen losing control of the match.

Augsburg thought they had scored the 3-0 in the 41st minute when Keitel slotted home off a quick throw-in. Petersen nevertheless ruled that FCA defender Bah had fouled Mainz counterpart Kacper Potulski in the lead-up. Petersen revealed restraint by not booking the crowd of Augsburg players who stood before him to protest his decision, but offered head coach Baum no such quarter when he kept Nadiem Amiri from executing a throw-in in the 43rd. Baum kept the ball himself whilst protesting to Petersen. The FCA trainer was promptly ejected from proceedings on a straight red.

In a recent development, petersen found himself at the center of more protests from players before it was time to head into the tunnel. The hosts were not pleased when the referee declined to whistle for a shove by Posch on Claude-Maurice just outside the box during first-half injury time. Prior to that, Petersen was compelled by VAR to take another look at a Fellhauer foul on Sano in the 44th. Petersen initially only awarded a yellow card despite the fact that Fellhauer caught Sano on the knee with his swinging boot. Petersen stood by his decision and was surely pleased to retreat to the tunnel after a heated, scrappy, and contentious end to the half.

To the relief of most observers, the focus returned to football after the change of ends. There would be no controversy attached to either of the goals scored in the opening five minutes of the second half. The hosts added their third goal shortly after play resumed. A free-kick delivery from the right was initially cleared before Behrens headed the ball back into the penalty area. Wolf helped it onward, and Posch inadvertently glanced the ball into Gregoritsch’s path in the 48th minute. The Austrian striker stroked home the 3-0. Fischer’s team responded by pulling a goal back promptly, with halftime sub Königsdörffer polishing off a nice distance effort on a quick counter three minutes later.

Königsdörffer’s 3-1 worked wonders for the carnival club’s confidence, and Fischer’s men undeniably looked more assured heading forward for the duration of proceedings. Mainz tightened up the possession statistics and looked more inspired when forging ahead. The more optically pleasing football from Mainz nevertheless didn’t end up producing another goal or even another memorable attempt on target. Instead, it was Augsburg who looked more dangerous on the counter. FCA sub Uchenna Ogundu unluckily missed out on the 4-1 with a strike off the inside of the far post in the 81st.

Finn Dahmen (5) – Juma Bah (6), Yannik Keitel (6), Tim Schnitzer (6) – Marius Wolf (6), Robin Fellhauer (6), Fabian Rieder (6), Hennes Behrens (5) – Anton Kade (6), Alexis Claude-Maurice (5) – Michael Gregoritsch (7).

Substitutes: Arijon Ibrahimovic (6), Uchenna Ogundu (6), Young-Woo Seol (-), Mert Kömür (-).

Robin Zentner (4) – Danny da Costa (5), Stefan Posch (1), Kacper Potulski (6), Anthony Caci (5) – Kaishu Sano (5), Phillipp Mwene (6) – Paul Nebel (4), Nadiem Amiri (3), Sheraldo Becker (4) – Phillip Tietz (4).

Substitutes: Ransford Königsdörffer (7), Benedict Hollerbach (6), Silvan Widmer (6), Eric Martel (-), Rael Nakuzola (-).

Industry observers note that the Austrian international proved the difference-maker with an exceptionally efficient performance in front of goal. Gregoritsch scored twice from just three shots, putting both of his efforts on target past Robin Zentner and outperforming his 1.36 xG. The 31-year-old wasn’t particularly involved in Augsburg’s build-up play, registering just 26 touches and completing 56 percent of his passes during his 72 minutes on the pitch. Gregoritsch nevertheless demonstrated precisely why Baum continues to place his faith in him. The veteran striker’s opportunistic finishing on both goals helped Augsburg snap their seven-match winless streak and lifted his Bundesliga tally to six goals for the season.

GGFN | Peter Weis – reporting from the WWK Arena.

Augsburg homegrown talent Tim Schnitzer seizes opportunity in vital Bundesliga win

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Eighteen-year-old FC Augsburg academy prospect Tim Schnitzer enjoyed an unforgettable afternoon on Sunday, making his first Bundesliga start in his hometown club’s 3-1 victory over Mainz 05.
  • Speaking to Get German Football News and other journalists in the mixed zone after the match, Schnitzer called it a “dream come true to start where I used to be a ball boy”.
  • “I was definitely a little nervous,” Schnitzer conceded.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eighteen-year-old FC Augsburg academy prospect Tim Schnitzer enjoyed an unforgettable afternoon on Sunday, making his first Bundesliga start in his hometown club’s 3-1 victory over Mainz 05. A defensive injury crisis forced head coach Manuel Baum to deploy the youngster in an unfamiliar role, but Schnitzer delivered an impressively composed performance that earned special praise from his trainer.

Speaking to Get German Football News and other journalists in the mixed zone after the match, Schnitzer called it a “dream come true to start where I used to be a ball boy”. The Augsburg native admitted to some nervousness ahead of his starting XI debut. Schnitzer revealed that he had slept less than usual the night before and even awoken before his alarm clock.

“I was definitely a little nervous,” Schnitzer conceded.

The Germany youth international nevertheless settled into his role on the left side of Augsburg’s back-three relatively rapidly, displaying maturity and confidence in possession. Schnitzer won 70 percent of his ground challenges and connected with 89 percent of his passes, according to Opta data.

GGFN considered Schnitzer and the rest of the makeshift back-three (consisting of Schnitzer’s fellow out-of-position player Yannik Keitel and young Man City loanee Juma Bah) worthy of above average marks in our player ratings piece.

“When you seize your chance, you become more and more integrated into the team,” Schnitzer remarked in the mixed zone.

Augsburg’s defensive personnel shortage left Baum with little choice but to turn to the 18-year-old, who ordinarily operates as a defensive midfielder. Chrislain Matsima, Jeffrey Gouweleeuw, Noahkai Banks, and Calvin Brackelmann were all unavailable, leaving the returning Juma Bah as the only other natural central defender available to the FCA trainer.

“We were missing four central defenders and were still able to field a back-three,” Baum remarked at the post-match press conference. “And I believe we were able to implement something that we always aim for as a club. Namely, to integrate young players in at the right moment. And we witnessed that with Tim Schnitzer, who delivered a fabulous performance in his first game and the team really helped him out with that.”.

Recent findings suggest that “A huge compliment to the whole team,” Baum continued near the end of his opening press conference statement. “And let’s single out Tim again. He’s from our own academy and has been with us since the U9s. I think he grew up just a couple of blocks away from the academy. I think we can be very happy about the result, the team, and the next homegrown talent who was able to start today.”.

Schnitzer’s first Bundesliga start represents another significant milestone in a development pathway that Get German Football News has followed closely since the summer. The Augsburg-born midfielder made his senior debut against RB Leipzig last March before spending the summer attempting to establish himself as a genuine first-team option. Schnitzer’s versatility emerged as one of his most promising qualities, with the youngster capable of operating as a defensive midfielder, central defender, or No. 8.

Baum had already identified Schnitzer as one of Augsburg’s most promising academy graduates in August, even mentioning the teenager among several FCA players he hoped might eventually attract Germany senior national-team consideration. Our 2026/27 Augsburg tactical preview also highlighted Schnitzer’s encouraging preseason performances, including his goal against Bournemouth, and suggested that the youngster should have opportunities to collect meaningful Bundesliga minutes.

It has been revealed that sunday’s injury-enforced selection certainly provided one such opportunity. Schnitzer responded by completing the entire 90 minutes and helping Augsburg end their seven-match winless streak. Whether the teenager retains his place once Augsburg’s established defenders return remains to be seen. Baum nevertheless has another option at his disposal, and the youngster who once served as a ball boy at the WWK Arena has taken another important step toward becoming a Bundesliga regular.

GGFN | Peter Weis – reporting from the WWK Arena.

Industry News: Augsburg’s Manuel Baum questions rulebook’s double standard after seeing red in Bundesliga win

💡 Key Takeaways
  • FC Augsburg head coach Manuel Baum has questioned the severity of the straight red card he received during Sunday’s 3-1 Bundesliga victory over Mainz 05, while acknowledging that referee Martin Petersen acted in accordance with the rules.
  • Recent findings suggest that augsburg, already leading 2-0, thought they had added a third goal when Yannik Keitel finished from close range following a throw-in.
  • “The 3-0 should have been legitimate and in accordance with the rules,” Baum remarked at the post-match press conference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

FC Augsburg head coach Manuel Baum has questioned the severity of the straight red card he received during Sunday’s 3-1 Bundesliga victory over Mainz 05, while acknowledging that referee Martin Petersen acted in accordance with the rules. The FCA trainer was dismissed in the 43rd minute following a heated sequence of events toward the end of the first half.

Recent findings suggest that augsburg, already leading 2-0, thought they had added a third goal when Yannik Keitel finished from close range following a throw-in. Petersen nevertheless disallowed the goal for a foul on Mainz defender Kacper Potulski in the build-up. Baum’s frustration with the decision ultimately led to his dismissal. The 47-year-old held onto the ball as Mainz midfielder Nadiem Amiri attempted to execute a quick throw-in.

“The 3-0 should have been legitimate and in accordance with the rules,” Baum remarked at the post-match press conference. “We’ve been informed afterwards that it should have counted. The ball came to me and I held onto it because I wanted to have a word with the ref and, I only noticed on the replay that I moved it from my left to right hand [while Nadiem Amiri was trying to execute a quick throw in].”.

Recent findings suggest that under IFAB Law 12, a team official who delays the opposition’s restart by holding onto the ball commits a sending-off offence. Players, by contrast, are generally cautioned for delaying a restart. Baum acknowledged that Petersen’s decision was technically correct but suggested that the rules impose an unnecessarily harsh punishment on coaches.

It has been revealed that “According to the rules, the coach must be punished draconically in such a case,” Baum continued. “A player would be given a yellow. A coach must automatically be given a red for such a thing. What? I find that a little strange. I think a yellow card would have been sufficient. But, okay. That’s the letter of the law. The team, I think did a great job of disengaging themselves from the emotions in the game and seeing it through.”.

It has been revealed that despite losing their head coach before halftime, Augsburg successfully protected their advantage and ultimately ended a seven-match winless Bundesliga streak. Michael Gregoritsch completed his brace shortly after the restart, and the hosts held firm after Mainz substitute Ransford Königsdörffer pulled a goal back.

Recent findings suggest that FC Augsburg head coach Manuel Baum has praised the contributions of his younger players following Sunday’s 3-1 Bundesliga victory over Mainz 05. Two of Augsburg’s promising young African talents have now scored their first Bundesliga goals on successive matchdays, with Manchester City loanee Juma Bah and Nigerian striker Uchenna Ogundu both making their mark in recent weeks.

Recent findings suggest that bah, 20, scored Augsburg’s second goal against Mainz, while fellow youngster Tim Schnitzer, 18, impressed on his first Bundesliga start. Ogundu, also 20, nearly added a fourth goal after entering as a substitute, striking the inside of the far post in the 81st minute. Asked about Bah’s performance at the post-match press conference, Baum took the opportunity to highlight the youthful composition of his team.

Recent findings suggest that “If you look back there, it looked like a child’s sweet shop today with Hennes [Behrens, 21], Tim Schnitzer [18], Juma Bah [20],” Baum responded. “Even Yannick Keitel [26] is still young. Marius [Wolf] was the most experienced player.”.

In a recent development, “The nice thing about seeing players like Juma and others back there is that, despite their age, they’re able to gain experience with us,” Baum continued. “And one sees what youngsters can achieve when they have a certain level of confidence. Uchi [Uchenna Ugundu, 20] also came in today and hit the post.”.

Bah’s goal represented an important personal milestone for the Sierra Leone international, who returned from suspension to help Baum contend with the absences of Jeffrey Gouweleeuw, Chrislain Matsima, Noahkai Banks, and Calvin Brackelmann.

As Get German Football News reported when Bah completed his loan move from Manchester City in September, Augsburg secured a purchase option reportedly worth €21.5m for the young defender. Bah arrived with considerable senior experience from previous spells at Lens and Nice, but has faced competition for playing time in the Bavarian Swabian defence.

Sunday’s performance offered another indication of what the club hopes to gain from the arrangement. Bah bundled home following Fabian Rieder’s 36th-minute corner to double Augsburg’s advantage and helped the makeshift back-three protect the lead.

According to recent reports, ogundu’s first Bundesliga goal came a fortnight earlier, with the Nigerian polishing off a Fabian Rieder through ball in second-half injury time of Augsburg’s 5-2 defeat to RB Leipzig. Speaking in an interview published in Augsburg’s matchday programme ahead of Sunday’s Mainz encounter, Ogundu described the goal as a proud personal moment, albeit one tempered by the disappointing result.

The 20-year-old identified his speed as his greatest asset and expressed satisfaction with his technical and tactical development since arriving in the Bundesliga. Ogundu also spoke of the support he has received from his teammates, singling out Keitel, Michael Gregoritsch, and Behrens as particularly helpful in making him feel at home in the Fuggerstadt.

In a recent development, the Nigerian, whom GGFN covered extensively following his expensive winter transfer from Alanyaspor, arrived in Augsburg amid stiff competition for places in attack. Our 2026/27 Augsburg tactical preview identified Ogundu as one of the winners of preseason preparations, while cautioning that his opportunities would remain limited by the presence of more established attacking options.

Recent findings suggest that his first Bundesliga goal and lively substitute appearance against Mainz nevertheless suggest that Ogundu is beginning to make a stronger case for playing time. Baum’s comments suggest that the FCA trainer remains encouraged by the progress of his younger players. With Schnitzer also delivering an impressive starting XI debut, Sunday’s victory provided Augsburg with more than just a welcome three points.

The injury crisis may have forced Baum’s hand, but the performances of his emerging talents have offered him several additional options moving forward.

In a recent development, konsa makes an notable challenge on the relentless Brobbey, as does Gabriel on Le Fee a few seconds later. Sunderland keep pushing and Sadiki rakes a shot over the bar from the edge of the area.

Sources indicate that chance for Sunderland A long throw from the right isn’t cleared by Arsenal, and eventually Meunier hits a snapshot that is kicked away instinctively by David Raya. That’s a pretty good save.

We’re off again at the Stadium of Light.

Jurrien Timber and Bruno Guimaraes, who is popular in these parts, replace Ben White and Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Tzolis’s deep cross is headed back into the six-yard box by Saka. Havertz stoops towards the ball but is beaten to it by Xhaka, a crucial bit of defending and the last action of a hard-fought, goalless first half.

Ben White has a groin problem and is going to be replaced by Jurrien Timber, either now or at half-time.

Sources indicate that xhaka’s dangerous corner is punched back to him by Raya. He picks out Le Fee, who drags a shot wide of the near post from 20 yards. Sunderland’s belief is growing.

Angulo goes down in the Arsenal area after a challenge from the side by White. Play continues and Meunier’s speuclative shot deflects behind for a corner.

Sunderland have been terrific in this first half.

Sources indicate that mikel Arteta is booked for encroaching outside his technical area. He responds by sticking his thumb up at the fourth official.

Mikel Arteta receives a yellow card for stepping out of the technical area 😅📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/xDlnL1B9MY.

Arsenal are yet to score from a set piece this season. Their supporters have used that fact as evidence they are not as reliant on corners as their critics say, but the truth is that it will bother Arteta and set-piece coach Nicolas Jover. This is the sort of cagey game in which Arsenal so often made the breakthrough from a set piece last season.

Sunderland break through Mukiele, who charges into space and rifles a low drive that is blocked by Gabriel on the edge of the area.

It has been revealed that the resulting corner leads to a brief VAR check for an Arsenal penalty after a bit of a wrestling match between Calafiori and Brobbey. Nothing given.

Good save by Roefs Saka curls a cross towards Havertz, who does well to control it on the chest while facing away from goal. He waits for the ball to bounce and hooks an imaginative shot that is fingertipped over by Roefs. Good save.

Industry observers note that chance for Arsenal Tzolis plays a nice pass down the side of the area for Odegaard. He cuts the ball back to Havertz, who screws a first-time shot over the bar. It was a slightly awkward chance because of the angle of Odegaard’s pass.

Reinildo is booked for a foul on Saka. The home fans are getting annoyed with what they perceive as diving from some of the Arsenal attackers: “Same old Arsenal, always cheating” is the chant of choice just now. Odegaard also went down a moment ago after a foul from Angulo.

Recent findings suggest that gabriel strides forward from defence and sweeps a left-foot shot from 25 yards. It’s a good effort that fades just wide of the far post with Roefs scrambling across his line.

Sunderland will be really pleased with the first quarter. They’re defending solidly and look a threat on the break, thanks in part to some outstanding hold-up play from Brian Brobbey. Saka’s volley is the only shot on target at either end.

Sources indicate that chance for Sunderland Brobbey does brilliantly to hold the ball and find Le Fee, who is fouled on the left wing by Gabriel. That allows Sunderland to send the centre-backs forward - and one of them, Dan Ballard, almost opens the scoring!

Xhaka curled a sensational ball around the Arsenal defence towards the far post, where the ball bounced up awkwardly and was knocked wide by either Ballard or Mukiele, who flew in at the far post. Ballard would have had an easier chance had Mukiele not got in the way.

In a recent development, chance for Arsenal Saka mishits a volley straight at Roefs from close range after running onto a penetrative pass from Rice. It wasn’t an easy ball to take on the volley - Rice hit it very firmly - but Saka would usually do better.

The pattern of the game has been established, with Arsenal dominating the ball and Sunderland picking their moments to press and then counter-attack.

Looks like it will be a good battle between Brian Brobbey and Ezri Konsa. Brobbey seems to be attaching himself to Konsa, rather than getting into a scrap with Gabriel.

According to recent reports, sunderland break promisingly down the right. Mukiele drives an angled low cross that only just evades Angulo at the far post.

Calafiori has a shot from 18 yards blocked after a typical run infield from left-back.

In a recent development, enzo Le Fee tries to score from inside his own half. David Raya was outside the penalty area but Le Fee completely mishit the shot.

In a recent development, arsenal have started well and are dominating possession. So far it’s all been in front of the Sunderland defence, but you’d expect that to change if they continue to have this much of the ball.

The champions kick off from left to right as we watch.

There’s a pulsating atmosphere at the Stadium of Light - you’d expect nothing less - and the action is about to begin.

Myles Lewis Skelly is the first England teenager to start the first four league games of a season for Arsenal since Tony Adams and David Rocastle in the 1986/87 campaign.

Recent findings suggest that we’re in a congested period right now. We’re playing midweek games as well. We made four changes against Napoli, we make another four for today and we try to keep all the players connected with a high level of confidence, and with the right chemistry in and around the team.

In a recent development, we know how tough Sunderland made it for every opponent here [last season] and we know the beautiful atmosphere that they create, the organisation that they have and the individuals that they have. We’ll try to impose ourselves like we always do and come here and be as dominant as we’ve been and then be ready to win the game.

Industry observers note that arsenal’s biggest rivals are still waiting for their first win - and their first goal - of the Premier League season. Alex Connor has reaction to their 0-0 draw at home to Everton.

"For sure we can improve, and we will" 😅Mikel Arteta on Arsenal's strong start to the season 🗣️📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nDpwooZq4Y.

Arsenal keeper David Raya has conceded only one goal in five matches this season, but he was beaten twice on this ground last season during a thrilling 2-2 draw.

Recent findings suggest that when will Martin Zubimendi start again for Arsenal? Mikel Arteta wants to avoid a repeat of last season, when Zubimendi played more games than anyone in Europe, but it is curious that the Spaniard has not yet started a single match of this campaign. It is one thing to reduce his minutes, and another to turn him into a permanent substitute.

Zubimendi has looked quite good off the bench in recent games but has been behind Myles Lewis-Skelly and Mikel Merino in the battle to partner Declan Rice from the start. And that’s before Bruno Guimaraes, the upcoming £75m signing, reaches full fitness.

Industry observers note that in the thick Naples air in midweek, Declan Rice did what he always does: he kept running. Another start for the Arsenal midfielder, another 90 minutes completed and another performance of constructive passing and destructive defending. For anyone who was worried about Rice’s physical condition, it was an emphatic response.

According to recent reports, after that Champions League victory over Napoli, Rice insisted he was ready for another marathon campaign. He made 69 appearances for club and country last season, up from 60 the previous term, and believes that is a sustainable number of games, even for an all-action midfielder such as himself. “I have shown I can do it,” he remarked.

The key question, though, is not whether Rice can do it, but whether he should do it. There is no doubt that his body eventually began to pay the price for his exertions last year, especially during the World Cup, and it would be reasonable for his managers to worry that his extraordinary workload might one day take a serious toll. This, after all, is a footballer who managed nerve pain in his hamstring throughout the second half of last season.

Regis Le Bris, who made 11 changes for the League Cup win over Hull in midweek, reverts to the starting XI that drew at Brentford seven days ago.

It has been revealed that RLB's XI to take on Arsenal! ❤️👊#SUNARS pic.twitter.com/F1nXWky4Fp.

Mikel Arteta has made four changes to the Arsenal team that won in Napoli during the week. Kai Havertz’s return is the headline news in Arteta’s selection, with in-form left-back Riccardo Calafiori also returning. Myles Lewis-Skelly returns to the midfield and Christos Tzolis starts.

🟡 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🔵 Your Saturday night Gunners ❤️‍🔥🤝 Presented by @deel.

It has been revealed that hello and welcome to live, minute-by-minute coverage of Sunderland v Arsenal at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

There’s a long way to go, and Arsenal fans will remember how blisteringly they started their last two title defences in 2002-03 and 2004-05, only to ultimately fall short. But right now, they could barely be in better shape. Their fine start to the season came with a Champions League win in Naples, achieved despite a delay to their flight from London.

According to recent reports, “I love those challenges,” said Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”.

Recent findings suggest that arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”.

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

Ruben Amorim, allenatore del Milan, è presente in conferenza stampa al termine di Milan-Frosinone, sfida valida per la dodicesima giornata di Serie A.

Sources indicate that “Oggi la partita non è stata solo una questione tattica. Si sono visti cambi di posizione, uno contro uno con tantissimo spazio: sembrava una gara pazza. Quello che ho percepito contro il Genoa e nelle altre partite è che eravamo troppo lontani, non arrivavamo nell'ultimo terzo di campo. Non siamo come le massive: se guardate le grandi squadre, per esempio la Juventus, magari fatica nei risultati, ma vedete il volume che produce. Per noi è un po' l'opposto, quindi sono davvero preoccupato che, se non miglioriamo, non potremo mantenere questo numero di punti. Oggi però è stato un passo avanti: si sono visti tanti giocatori attaccare la profondità, cosa che non si era vista contro il Ferencvaros. Nelle altre gare avevamo gestito bene il pallone, ma oggi servivano ritmo e corse. Dobbiamo riuscire a giocare entrambe le partite all'interno della stessa gara, ma oggi era chiaramente il tipo di partita che dovevamo fare per vincere. Oggi non è stata una questione di allenatore, credo, ma di giocatori. E loro, visto che si giocava uomo contro uomo, dovevano solo fare quello che riescono a fare quando sono così bravi: saltare l'uomo e aprire lo spazio. Quindi oggi il merito è tutto dei giocatori.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • This would seem like an obvious thing to say after Harry Kane was ruled out for the next three months with an ankle injury,, while Luis Diaz, Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry are also out injured, but this has been a problem for most of the season too, and these injuries are likely to make the matter worse.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Bundesliga returned following the final international break of the year, and what a spectacle it was. From a swing of the title race pendulum, to changes at the bottom of the table, Get German Football News has you covered with the latest talking points after Matchday 10.

Here are five things we learned….

This would seem like an obvious thing to say after Harry Kane was ruled out for the next three months with an ankle injury,, while Luis Diaz, Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry are also out injured, but this has been a problem for most of the season too, and these injuries are likely to make the matter worse.

Even with Kane fit, Bayern have been wasteful in front of goal this season. Granted, some of the results the ball just wouldn’t go in, like against Schalke and Augsburg, but the difference between this season and last year was that Bayern would prove to be far more clinical in front of goal, but Germany’s record champions seemed to have lost that edge now, as shown in their 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday night.

This has resulted in games where Bayern should win comfortably being a lot more difficult, mainly due to their own doing. With the injury to Kane, and with no fit back-up, this problem is likely to get worse and could make or break Bayern’s Bundesliga season. It’s now up to Vincent Kompany and his coaching team to find a solution, and quick.

Usually after Bayern drop points, Dortmund fail to capitalise, and ultimately, nothing would change. However, Matchday 10 was different.

It has been revealed that naturally, Dortmund did not make it easy for themselves against last-placed Borussia Mönchengladbach as they struggled to break down Alexander Blessin’s side, while Felix Nmecha’s winner in the 80th minute came from a mistake by Gladbach keeper Daniel Batz. But a win is a win, and Dortmund are now top of the Bundesliga with a two-point lead over Bayern.

Considering how this has been a problem for Dortmund before, it goes to show the effect that Niko Kovač is having on the side, that they are able to win these types of games – and to win ugly, especially when they have previously struggled in the past. Their latest 1-0 victory is already the third of its kind this season.

We probably now have a title race on our hands.

While the move is still technically a loan, it is more than likely that RB Leipzig will make the signing of Brajan Gruda permanent, and they will have to do their best not to immediately flip him for what will be a healthy profit.

Since returning to Leipzig in the summer, Gruda has been one of Leipzig’s standout players, like Antonio Nusa and Christopher Nkunku. The 22-year-old only made his Germany debut in the recent international break, but he immediately hit the ground running under Jürgen Klopp – where he recorded two goals and provided two assists against Serbia and the Netherlands – while also continuing his Bundesliga form.

The winger scored his first Bundesliga goal of the season in Leipzig’s 5-1 rout against Union Berlin, while also providing the assist for Leipzig’s second goal of the day. In the opening stages of the season, it looked as if Leipzig were missing Yan Diomande, but Gruda has replaced the now Real Madrid player with relative ease.

Recent findings suggest that while, on paper, a 0-0 draw against UEFA Champions League participants VfB Stuttgart is a good result, fans will certainly feel uneasy at their precarious position in the Bundesliga. The Royal Blues’ draw and Union Berlin’s 5-1 defeat against RB Leipzig sees Miron Muslic’s charges climb into the promotion/relegation play-off, but the fact that they are yet to score at the Veltins Arena is a worrying one.

No team has scored fewer than their five goals in ten games this season and with games against fellow Bundesliga returnees Paderborn, Revierderby rivals Borussia Dortmund, Hamburg and Borussia Mönchengladbach, it’s difficult to see where goals will arrive from.

According to recent reports, after a 4-1 defeat against Freiburg on Matchday 1, few gave Werder Bremen little chance of remaining in the division this season, especially given the departures of Mio Backhaus and Romano Schmid, long-term injury to Jens Stage, and being somewhat light up top. But, the impressive team cohesion intertwined with Niclas Füllkrug’s timely return has made the Green-Whites incredibly fun to watch.

Füllkrug struck his tenth Bundesliga goal of the season, and Bremen’s fourth against Hamburg in the Bundesliga’s 111th Nordderby, as Daniel Thioune’s charges secured bragging rights over their northern rivals – a timely present for the head coach that had just signed a contract extension.

Sitting sixth, Bremen have turned the Weserstadion into a fortress, where they remain unbeaten with four wins and a draw in the Bundesliga this season, which places them three points clear of chasing Eintracht Frankfurt. While free-scoring RB Leipzig and well-ran Freiburg are deservedly in the top four, they’ll be rightly looking in their rear view mirror to see Bremen hunting them down.

Il mister Gennaro Gattuso ha rilasciato delle dichiarazioni ai microfoni di Dazn e LSC poco dopo il fischio finale di Lazio-Lecce, terminato 3-0 grazie alla doppietta di Noslin e alla rete di Frattesi.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Non siamo partiti benissimo, eravamo appannati, poi la squadra ha fatto bene. Lecce scomodo, ti giocano addosso, non è stato semplice ma sono orgoglioso per mentalità e voglia. Ieri avevo detto di non essere preoccupato, li vedo in settimana, oggi hanno giocato Leite, Doekhi e Pedraza che non avevano mai giocato insieme ma ero tranquillo perché li vedo quando arrivano in campo, c'è grande spirito e dobbiamo continuare così. A destra giochiamo in un modo e a sinistra in un altro, Taylor ci dà qualità, è merito dei ragazzi che ci stanno mettendo tantissima mentalità e senso di appartenenza. Diamo merito a questi ragazzi, stanno facendo qualcosa di incredibile.

Sources indicate that rovella? Può dare più verticalizzazione, ci darà una mano. Ora possiamo anche fare 4-2-3-1, poi vedremo. Dele-Bashiru meriterebbe di più, abbiamo diversi giocatori. Ora servono minuti nelle gambe a Rovella che è mancato per tantissimo tempo, è un giocatore importante. Cosa manca? Sbagliare ci sta, giochiamo a velocità alte, mi interessa la mentalità ed è una sorpresa come stiamo tenendo botta. Sono soddisfatto, si vuole sempre qualcosa in più ma con questi ritmi gli errori tecnici ci possono stare. Non siamo stati sempre precisi, possiamo migliorare nella lettura delle partite.

Recent findings suggest that dimmi quando è una partita facile? Non esistono. Ci hanno messo in difficoltà i primi 10/15 minuti, quando si abbassava Reda e i due braccetti. Ci chiudevano le giocate, dopo sulle seconde palle squadra troppo verticale. Il primo tempo abbiamo avuto sei o sette calci d’angolo. Il secondo tempo siamo entrati con un piglio diverso, mi ha sorpreso la mentalità ancora una volta. Abbiamo trovato spazio dentro nel secondo tempo, dovevamo andare più verticali anche noi. Anche Noslin, al di là dei gol, ha sbagliato tanto oggi.

C’era Pedraza al 70° che non ne poteva più. Non ero preoccupato, oggi abbiamo cambiato tre giocatori che non hanno mai giocato insieme, ma quando vedi come si allenano in settimana ci sta che uno può giocare meno bene ma questa squadra c’ha gamba e lo hanno dimostrato.

La soddisfazione più grande, merito loro. Il fatto di farsi trovare pronti e giocare partite in questo modo è una grande soddisfazione. Alla fine quando le cose vanno bene, perché nel secondo tempo abbiamo rischiato poco e li abbiamo tenuti là, fai fatica a cambiare quando è così. Ti viene il braccino. La motivazione è questa. In quel momento non sapevo chi togliere perché vedevo una squadra ben messa in campo.

Atalanta-Inter risultato finale 4-4: l'Inter spreca e viene agguantata nel finale

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2009 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fcinter1908

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Una serata che sembrava destinata a trasformarsi in una festa nerazzurra si chiude con un pareggio dal sapore amarissimo.
  • L'Inter parte con personalità e trova il vantaggio al 16' con Pio Esposito, bravo a coordinarsi in area e superare Sportiello.
  • Industry observers note that nella ripresa l'Inter sembra prendere definitivamente il controllo dell'incontro.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Una serata che sembrava destinata a trasformarsi in una festa nerazzurra si chiude con un pareggio dal sapore amarissimo. L'Inter di Cristian Chivu non va oltre il 4-4 sul campo dell'Atalanta, al termine di una partita spettacolare, ricca di gol e continui ribaltamenti. Protagonista assoluto Francesco Pio Esposito, autore di una straordinaria tripletta, che però non basta alla squadra milanese per conquistare tre punti pesantissimi. L'Atalanta di Sarri ha il merito di non arrendersi mai, trovando il pareggio proprio nel finale con Kessie.

L'Inter parte con personalità e trova il vantaggio al 16' con Pio Esposito, bravo a coordinarsi in area e superare Sportiello. Il giovane attaccante è scatenato e al 32' firma anche il raddoppio, questa volta con un colpo di testa sugli sviluppi di un calcio d'angolo. La gioia nerazzurra viene però parzialmente ridimensionata dall'uscita per infortunio di Calhanoglu, sostituito da Sucic, e dalla rete di Elmas che al 35' riporta l'Atalanta in partita. Si va così all'intervallo sul risultato di 2-1 per la formazione di Chivu.

Industry observers note that nella ripresa l'Inter sembra prendere definitivamente il controllo dell'incontro. Al 52' Thuram inventa una splendida giocata e serve Pio Esposito, che davanti a Sportiello non sbaglia e completa la sua tripletta personale. Sul 3-1 la partita sembra indirizzata, ma l'Atalanta trova la forza per reagire. Al 71' De Ketelaere accorcia le distanze sugli sviluppi di un calcio d'angolo. Cinque minuti più tardi Sucic, dal dischetto, restituisce all'Inter il doppio vantaggio, portando il risultato sul 4-2.

Neppure il quarto gol, però, basta a mettere al sicuro la vittoria. All'81' De Ketelaere approfitta di una respinta corta di Pavard e firma la propria doppietta, riaprendo nuovamente una sfida che sembrava chiusa. L'Atalanta continua a spingere, mentre l'Inter fatica a gestire il vantaggio. Nel finale arriva l'episodio decisivo: fallo di mano di Bastoni in area, calcio di rigore per i bergamaschi e trasformazione di Kessie al 90' per il definitivo 4-4.

It has been revealed that per Chivu resta una serata dai due volti. Da una parte la prestazione straordinaria di Pio Esposito e la capacità della squadra di costruire occasioni e segnare quattro reti su un campo difficile. Sicuramente abbiamo iniziato l'anno con un mister nuovo, con idee nuove, quindi non è semplice, però abbiamo giocatori forti e potremo sicuramente competere".

Massimiliano Allegri, allenatore del Napoli, è intervenuto ai microfoni di Sky Sport dopo la vittoria contro il Torino: “Segnano solo se sorridono? Diciamo che non c’era il mood giusto. Abbiamo tante azioni senza concretizzare. Allora io ho detto: ‘Sorridiamo, così facciamo gol!’. Vincere le partite non è facile. Sicuramente dobbiamo migliorare alcune situazioni, difendere sui calci d’angolo e sulle palle inattive. De Bruyne? Pensavo che vicino alla punta potesse far meglio ed è andata così. Hojlund? Credo che abbia disputato una buona partita, si è messo a disposizione della squadra. La squadra, fino a questo momento, ha disputato delle buone partite creando molto. Ci è forse mancata la cattiveria di difendere. Hojlund ha creato e ha fatto molti tiri in porta. Per noi è un giocatore molto importante e utile per noi. Cosa ho detto a McTominay? Di non farsi trovare dietro ad Hojlund in posizione verticale, perché veniva marcato. Quando si è posizionato bene stando fermo, ha avuto più difficoltà. Nel secondo tempo si è mosso tra le linee ed è stato più bravo. Manchester City? E’ una sfida molto importante, ma sono le ultime partite quelle in cui ci giochiamo la qualificazione. Dobbiamo fare una bella partita all’Etihad, cercando di fare risultato, ma dobbiamo dare importanza al campionato”.

Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under big pressure

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that this was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United.
  • They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.
  • Industry observers note that but then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that this was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United. Not once. But twice. And, then, most painfully, a third time with a dismal, dispiriting defeat.

They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.

Industry observers note that but then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals. And that was a far more painful and damaging blow.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

On a day in which thousands of fans protested, accusing co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers – with Avram Glazer joining Ratcliffe in attendance – of treating them like “s---”, United unfortunately left a nasty whiff of being just that out on the pitch.

Sources indicate that united were frankly, woeful. They lacked belief and imagination and attacking instinct and too many of their players – their apparent major players – went missing when they needed to stand up and take the game by the scruff of the neck. They could not break down City’s defence and failed to be a front-foot team who can dominate the ball. Which is surely what they aspire to be?

It has been revealed that they hit the post twice – through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – with efforts from 25 yards. And those two local lads were by far their best players. Without them, United carried so little threat, were so blunt, that it was shocking.

Recent findings suggest that the question for Michael Carrick, the Manchester United head coach, is simple: what is he trying to do with this team? Can they only ever depend on counter-attacks?

Afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical plan to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

Sources indicate that it was telling that so little did City’s latest head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their new head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

In a recent development, was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a big team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

According to recent reports, the former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

According to recent reports, there was controversy around the red card and the goal. There is no doubt Foden had to go. But what about Fernandes? He clearly kicked Foden as he was on the ground with the midfielder reacting instinctively, two-footing him in the gut.

It meant he became the first City player to be dismissed in a Manchester derby in the league since Bernardo Corradi in December 2006 and will be punished with a three-match ban for violent conduct.

To make matters worse for Foden, who missed out on the World Cup, it happened in front of Thomas Tuchel who names his England squad for the Nations League campaign on Friday.

Recent findings suggest that phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL.

And the goal? Initially it was ruled out for offside as Haaland superbly turned in Josko Gvardiol’s cross beyond the far post – he made that tricky finish look routine. But after a lengthy VAR check that decision was overturned by referee Michael Oliver.

According to recent reports, patrick Dorgu had played Haaland onside but the issue then was whether Fernández had touched the ball as he tried to reach the cross. He had not. But even if he had not, surely he was impeding Lisandro Martínez’s attempt to clear? He was certainly in the defender’s line of vision which fits the criteria for the offside to be given as it interfered with an opponent.

Industry observers note that united can understandably complain but they can have no excuse. The pressure, already, will be beginning to mount on Carrick with just four points from four league games and down in 13th place. With a Carabao Cup tie at home to Brighton in midweek and a trip to Fulham next Sunday before the international break, he needs wins.

“We’ve only got 10 men,” goaded the City fans as the game headed into added time and United can expect to hear that again and again. And again.

Recent findings suggest that even so, at the death, Bryan Mbeumo – as otherwise anonymous as Matheus Cunha – had the chance to equalise after being shrewdly picked out by Fernandes. He was excellently thwarted by Gianluigi Donnarumma. But Mbeumo was clear inside the penalty area and had to score. Not that United would have deserved it. There were boos at the end and understandably so. United were just not good enough.

It has been revealed that I’m confused. We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision. It’s more worrying about if that’s the interpretation of football now. If that’s the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that’s really worrying for me. It’s a staggering explanation.

The decision isn’t going to change the season, but it’s had a major impact on the game. That decision wasn’t on us today. It’s up to us to create and score after that. We had moments. Of course it’s up to us to do that, but significant moments in games like that have a big impact.

We did a lot of things well, it looked like we were growing well into the game. We looked dangerous. We’ll take the positives from the game today and move on well, but we’re not moving on lightly.

We could have created more. That’s an answer for us, but we could have. That’s our second defeat now, since I’ve been in charge, but we’re a good team and we’ll get back to wining ways.

The red card changed the proposal of the game but credit to the players because the effort, spirit and togetherness has been brilliant.

In a recent development, [On Foden’s red card] Can be a red card, but in the same action can be a red card for Bruno. It is what it is, we won.

Changed the plan for us, and changed the plan for them. They are unbelievable in transition, and the moment we are with 10 men we give them no transitions.

When you are able to win a game with 10 players it’s fantastic, when this game is a derby it’s even better.

Last year with Chelsea I had a player sent off here after three minutes, this year 25, hopefully next time we play against 11vs11!

According to recent reports, we always knew it was going to be a tough game. What happened with Phil at the start wasn’t good for us, but we stated at half-time it would make us feel better if we win and we’ve taken three points.

It just gives you more motivation to go on and get the points. It was really tough for us. We had to run more and fight more. We all shone, to a man, and we were brilliant.

In a recent development, he was offside and what I can’t understand is it’s the rules... I went there because he was in front of him because that’s why Haaland was free at the back.

According to recent reports, every season they come to our club and spend an hour and a half explaining the rules, and they seem so confident with that, and then you have five or six people making this mistake. It’s unacceptable.

We have to go home with this injustice.

Haaland speaking on Sky: “We had to go low which is not ideal, we like to keep the ball, to try to score goals but in these times you have to go a bit low and take your chances when possible. We managed to do that well and that reveals personality and character, to keep the ball away at Old Trafford with 10 men.”.

“We had to change the plan a bit, but Enzo gave us a plan where we could play to our different strengths and counter-attack a bit more. For me personally, I just had to be there, to try to wait for a chance, and if there’s a chance, I had to be ready to execute. We also needed fighters in the team, which we have plenty of. Look at our midfield - it’s something they like to do! I’m so, so proud of everyone.”.

And on Donnarumma’s late save: “This wolf in goal giving you so much confidence, he looks a bit like a wolf. He is a mad man but he is a match-winner as well.”.

Recent findings suggest that 9 - Erling Haaland is now the top scorer in Premier League games between Manchester City and Manchester United:9 - Haaland (8 apps)8 - Agüero (13 apps)8 - Rooney (21 apps)Domination. pic.twitter.com/EBiifV12st.

City win the Old Trafford derby with 10 men and Enzo Maresca runs down the touchline to celebrate in front of the travelling fans while their players embrace Donnarumma after his late save.

There will be so much analysis of Foden’s red card, but more so how Haaland’s winner stood given the final result. Should Enzo Fernandez have been considered offside?

Recent findings suggest that but if you are judging performances, City are worthy winners. They defended stoutly, carried a threat and kept the ball well for periods even though they were a man light. United were aimless and froze.

A mammoth victory, and one which perhaps puts the breaks on talk of an Arsenal procession.

What a chance for Mbeumo to equalise! Superb save by Donnarumma, after the United forward was found by a Bruno Fernandes disguised pass into the box. Mbeumo took the ball under his spell and shot with power, but the substantial goalkeeper pushed the shot over the bar.

United have a corner, but Michael Oliver blows for a foul, and that is surely that.

Martinez tries a straight ball towards Sesko, which is too high for the striker. United have perhaps just one more attack in them if they are too salvage a point.

It has been revealed that dalot with another poor cross that flies over everyone in the penalty area. Then Mainoo’s pass in midfield is intercepted by Anderson, and Ndiaye can bring the ball forward for City until he his tackled buy Martinez.

Fernandes drifts a cross behind for a City goal kick, between Sesko and Zirkzee and it looks like United are running out of time and ideas.

Dorgu with another foul on Ndiaye, yet another break in play for City. And there are going to just FIVE minutes of added time, much to Old Trafford’s frustration.

It has been revealed that haaland does well to bring City forward after another United attack breaks down, and Dorgu is penalised for a foul on Ndiaye. Another stoppage follows because the ball hits Michael Oliver. City can see the finish line so, and they would deserve their three points.

Recent findings suggest that united have a corner after Guehi stands firm to block Cunha’s strike from distance. Maguire rises highest in the middle, but no United player gambled on the knockdown and his header drifts wide of the post.

It has been revealed that good work from Anderson against Mainoo in midfield, he receives a major cheer from the City fans. Carrick has thrown attackers on, but United have lost some structure and are not sustaining pressure.

Nico O’Reilly is now on for the closing stages, in place of Fernandez and Carrick has thrown on Zirkzee in place of Marcus Rashford. A United goal now would feel like a goal out of nowhere. City are playing the better football now and they have a corner.

United have lost all sense of momentum, City are keeping the ball for spells and then are happy for the game to be broken up stoppages.

Sources indicate that fernandez goes down looking for a penalty rather hopefully, and Maguire has been booked for his reaction as well as Fernandez for his role in the fracas. More and more time ticks away.

City are showing real resolve as well as quality here, Enzo Fernandez has just won a free-kick in the United half after a foul by Mainoo. The closest United have come in recent minutes was a glancing header wide from Mbeumo.

From that free-kick, Fernandez’s low delivery is close to being converted by Haaland or Guehi.

Sources indicate that it’s a major final 16 minutes here plus injuries for United. You’re at home to your derby rivals who have been down to 10 men since the 23rd minute and you’ve had just two players show up for the mostpart so far - Mainoo and Rashford. The rest are really going to have to lift it.

Fernandes stings the palms of Donnarumma with a strike from outside the box.

It has been revealed that we have now had an explanation and evidence of why the goal stood. The VAR check for offside on Haaland found that he was in fact onside by fine margins, and that Fernandez (who was offside) did not affect Lisandro Martinez as he threw himself at a diving header (and missed). The Fernandez element feels the more debatable.

Enzo Fernandes’s shot from the edge of the D is tipped on to the post by Lammens! United are living dangerously, and Carrick has now thrown Sesko on in place of Tielemans.

Haaland and his City team-mates run off to celebrate in front of the away fans including Noel Gallagher.

City with a better sequence of passing but it does Ndiaye cannot get a shot away and then Fernandez commits another foul in midfield. Cunha with a poor cross behind for a City goal kick.

And now sent off after 24 minutes.

A half that will be remembered for one thing and one thing only: Phil Foden’s red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.

United were shading things before that flashpoint, but City will be pleased with their response to the sending off. They have defended well, and posed a threat going forward without executing the final pass or shot.

Industry observers note that both teams adjusting after the red card, Cherki and Semenyo are trying to put in a defensive shift in front of their full-backs. United enjoying the majority of possession, and Fernandes feeds Rashford with a delightful reverse pass but Rashford’s first touch was loose.

United will now be favourites to win this game, but Mainoo was required to block a goal-bound strike from Cherki after a corner was clear. City do have the ammunition to offer a threat on the break. They need the Haaland of his Dortmund days to attack significant spaces on the counter.

Industry observers note that england manager Thomas Tuchel and his assistant Anthony Barry are among those in attendance at Old Trafford ahead of Friday’s squad announcement, the first since the World Cup and ahead of the forthcoming Nations League campaign. Cunha with a burst through City’s midfield and he is brought down by Fernandez. Promising counter-attack for United after Rashford pinches the ball off Foden in midfield, and the home team’s attacking quartet of players stream forward. Poor from Cunha though, dragging a shot well wide from an improbable distance.

Quite a composed start from City, Anderson enjoying plenty of touches in midfield. Fernandes tries to sweep a first-time pass out to Rashford wide left, but Nunes intercepts.

Free-kick for United in a crossing position right of centre, and from the second phase a Martinez cross flies into the gloves of Donnarumma.

An early glimpse of United’s slightly flimsy central midfield with Cherki finding space behind them and Enzo Fernandez’s strike from distance deflecting over the bar. Martinez heads Anderson’s delivery behind for another corner.

This time City take it short, but United clear their lines when the ball is crossed into the box.

The ball changes hands in midfield a couple of times in quick succession. Dalot pressing Semenyo but the winger gets away from him, but United win a challenge before Anderson nips in. Promising start if you want aggression and intensity.

United get the first Manchester derby of the season under way.

As expected, there is that banner above the mouth of the tunnel.

In some ways everything is on today, and it has to be, but it’s not everything in terms of the bigger picture.

Michael Carrick’s record has been outstanding, particularly at Old Trafford. They’ve been brilliant here and very difficult to beat.

If United drop points today, people will say it’s a bad start, if they win today, people will say they’re back.

And thousands have taken to the streets to voice their anger at how they feel they are being treated by the co-owners.

Plumes of red and green and yellow smoke filled the air as fans brandished banners and flags and chanted anti-Glazer and Ratcliffe songs.

They are now 2-0 down against Brighton and Taiwo Awoniyi has been sent off for an elbow. Bar a miracle, it will be zero points from four games for Frank Lampard’s team.

There will be no flags in the Stretford End today in a protest against ticketing policy which United say is about stopping touts, but loyal, innocent fans may have been caught in the crossfire. A crackdown has led to 685 supporters being stripped of their season tickets and another 464 being sanctioned. Sources indicate that both of these teams were in Champions League action this week but, as James Ducker explores in this piece, United have missed out in six of the last 13 campaigns. City have been ever-presents, with significant sporting and financial benefits. Over the 10 years between 2016 and 2025, City generated £343m more in broadcast revenue and prize money from European football than their derby rivals.

Sam Wallace was at Carrington this week to speak with Diogo Dalot, the Manchester United right-back who could make his 250th appearance for the club this afternoon. Dalot has been through some tumultuous times at Old Trafford, and is one of the great survivors in the squad. He talks about the scrutiny at United, his musical family and the negatives of social media for young players in an interview you can read here.

My sense is that while United fans generally understand and agree with the decision to stick with Carrick, they hope he is the long-term answer to get the club back to winning the Premier League or Champions League, while the rest of the world doubts it.

To most, it feels like Carrick remains an interim solution in all but name, entrusted with the keys to Old Trafford until a super coach can move in during the summer of 2027. Carrick will not see it that way, of course, but there are certain perceptions which will be tough to shake off.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the season’s first Manchester derby, with midfield rebuilds the theme of the summer on both sides of town.

Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi could all be involved for City, who lost Rodri and Bernardo Silva in the engine room, while United have recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in an attempt to address a long-standing problem.

Rodri’s departure and a Community Shield shellacking by Arsenal prompted some gloomy forecasts for Enzo Maresca and City, but confidence has grown since. The late turnaround at home to Bournemouth on the opening weekend could well look very key in a few months’ time, while Crystal Palace and Coventry have also been put away. Victory in Porto was probably Maresca’s most impressive result to date at City, though winning at Old Trafford would usurp that. Three points for City would mean they join Arsenal on a maximum of 12 points from four games.

It has been revealed that it has been a patchy start to the campaign for United and Michael Carrick, and this afternoon’s result will go a long way to shaping perceptions of where they are. The concession of a late equalise at Everton, in addition to a dreadful loss at Hull, adds a degree of pressure. United will be buoyed by their performance in this fixture in January, when they delivered possibly the best performance of the post-Ferguson years to slay City in a 2-0 win that could well have been four or five.

With Tielemans, Bruno Fernandes and Kobbie Mainoo prominent in midfield, United are trying to shift to a more possession-heavy approach, but any success against City in recent times has tended to come on the counter-attack. Maresca’s team have had lots of the ball in their first few games of the season, so that is the expected pattern again.Full team news on the way later.

Luca Marelli, ex arbitro, intervenuto a DAZN, ha analizzato i due rigori concessi da Maresca durante Atalanta-Inter di stasera: "Il primo rigore viene fischiato per un tocco di mano sulla linea di Zappacosta: è un episodio che va analizzato. Prima interviene col braccio e poi ancora con lo stesso: il primo tocco non è punibile, se non ci fosse stato il secondo tocco non lo sarebbe stato.

Quello punito è il secondo movimento: potrebbe essere istintivo per agevolare il portiere. L'arbitro decide per il giallo e io sono d'accordo: non è DOGSO perché il pallone non si stava più muovendo verso la porta e non ha impedito il concretizzarsi di un gol, ma è solo SPA perché ha impedito agli attaccanti di poter intervenire. Bastoni? Molto bravo Maresca, era in posizione perfetta: fischia perché le braccia erano sopra l'altezza della spalla, è sempre calcio di rigore.

According to recent reports, possiamo ipotizzare che abbiano protestato perché Bastoni era di spalle, ma ci soccorre la giurisprudenza recente. In Atalanta-Cagliari di un paio di mesi fa Orsato ci spiegò in un raduno a Lissone che quel fallo di mano è sempre punibile: lì la dinamica è un po' diversa, ma concettualmente simile perché Kolasinac colpisce col braccio sopra la spalla anche se è di spalle. E' quindi rigore anche stasera".

"A San Siro tutto bene. I rossoneri tornano in campo dopo due settimane di sosta e nella 12ª giornata di Serie A battono 5-1 il Frosinone. Risultato largo, prestazione positiva e tante reti: ad aprire le mercature è un'autorete di Calvani, poi torna al gol Gonçalo Ramos, nella ripresa segnano anche Jashari (il primo in rossonero!), Cisse e Pulisic. Terza vittoria consecutiva in campionato dopo quelle contro Inter e Genoa e quarto posto confermato con 27 punti. La sfida con il Frosinone si presentava come molto insidiosa, sono stati bravi e attenti i rossoneri ad interpretarla nel modo giusto.

According to recent reports, una serata da ricordare anche per Fondazione Milan, Match Charity Partner della partita (qui la gallery) e protagonista - insieme alle Legends rossonere Tassotti, Donadoni e Galli - di un emozionante tributo a Franco Baresi, pochi minuti prima del fischio d'inizio. Ora l'attenzione della squadra rossonera si sposta sulla 5ª giornata di Europa League, ad Atene contro l'Olympiacos giovedì 26 novembre alle 18.45, per riprendere il discorso nella competizione dopo due sconfitte di fila. Con questa stessa grinta e tanta voglia di far bene. Avanti ragazzi!".

Il mister Gennaro Gattuso ha rilasciato delle dichiarazioni in conferenza stampa poco dopo il fischio finale di Lazio-Lecce.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Mancano otto punti per fare la prima festa. Per il resto ne parleremo quando amncano 8-9 partite. Stupito sì, ma per la mentalità. I primi 15 minuti di oggi non sono andati benissimo, dopo molto meglio, abbiamo sofferto un po' sui nostri calci piazzati a favore. Eravamo un po' piantati sulle seconde palle. Secondo tempo molto orgogliosi della mentalità, della prestazione, non li abbiamo fatti respirare. Era da un po' di tempo che sbagliavamo sempre i secondi tempi, a questo giro siamo stati sul pezzo e li abbiamo messi in grandissima difficoltà.

Industry observers note that gattuso avrà un merito su quel che sta facendo la Lazio? Per come lavorano in allenamento. Ieri ero tranquillo, oggi abbiamo messo in campo Diogo, Pedraza,. La tranquillità me la danno i dati, il senso di appartenenza. Mi prendo questo merito: aver fatto diventare in pochissimo tempo questa squadra una famiglia.

Io ho giocato con otto palloni d'oro nella mia carriera. Taylor vede cose che gli altri non vedono. Gli altri avrebbero tirato di piattone, io sinceramente già lo stavo mandando a quel paese. Nel mio modo di pensare il calcio, quella giocata non m'è passata neanche per l'anticamera del cervello. Dico Rui Costa, dai.

Industry observers note that frattesi? Io non ho salvato la vita a nessuno. Lui è un capoccione, esagera sempre. Ha bisogno d'affetto, come tanti giocatori. Ha bisogno anche di prendere le mazzate nei denti, vuol giocare come dice lui. Il merito su quel che sta facendo è suo. Sono contento che abbia fatto gol di sinistro. Sono contento di tutti, sono felice di allenarli. Oggi mi dispiace che Dele abbia fatto 11 minuti, meriterebbe molto di più. Tanti altri meriterebbero di fare qualche minuto in più, si allenano in un modo incredibile.

Isaksen? Dentro non si passava oggi, dovevamo andare in verticale. L'abbiamo fatto pochissime volte, e quelle poche volte siamo rusciti a mettere pensiero. Anche Noslin oggi a livello tecnico ha sbagliato tanto. Isaksen è un piacere lavorare con lui, ha risolto i suoi problemi. Quest'estate l'abbiamo perso per un po', è un giocatore che riesce a fare delle cose in velocità. Ha la terza marcia con la palla al piede. Ha preso gusto a far gol, e anche a far assist. Ha fatto una partita incredibile anche con la Danimarca.

In a recent development, supercoppa? Per me è un regalo, io non c'entro nulla. Non è un impiccio, anzi. È una coppa. Manca un mese, pensa se possiamo pensare alla coppa. Quando arriverà, ci penseremo. Stai lì, provi a giocartela, giochi contro una squadra che sta dettando legge. Adesso recuperiamo due giorni e poi da martedì iniziano a preparare la sfida contro il Torino.

Qual è il segreto di questa Lazio? Noi proponiamo, però chi propone deve avere dall'altra parte gente che ci crede fortemente. Quando il giocatore la pensa in maniera diversa, lì viene il difficile. Bisogna esser bravi a fargli capire perché vogliamo fare determinate cose. Siamo stati bravi noi, sono bravi loro quando facciamo i lavori individuali. Con tutta questa organizzazione che abbiamo messo giù, loro si trovano bene. Noi proponiamo e per il momento tutto sta andando bene. La base di tutto è il lavoro: se vuoi giocare in questo modo qui, la fatica ti deve rimanere nella testa. A parlare è facile, non basta.

Dopo la vittoria del Milan di ieri pomeriggio contro il Frosinone in campionato, i rossoneri si rituferanno sulla Europa League per preparare la trasferta difficile e delicata ad Atene contro l'Olympiacos, in programma giovedì alle 18:45.

According to recent reports, "A San Siro tutto bene. I rossoneri tornano in campo dopo due settimane di sosta e nella 12ª giornata di Serie A battono 5-1 il Frosinone. Risultato largo, prestazione positiva e tante reti: ad aprire le mercature è un'autorete di Calvani, poi torna al gol Gonçalo Ramos, nella ripresa segnano anche Jashari (il primo in rossonero!), Cisse e Pulisic. Recent findings suggest that una serata da ricordare anche per Fondazione Milan, Match Charity Partner della partita (qui la gallery) e protagonista - insieme alle Legends rossonere Tassotti, Donadoni e Galli - di un emozionante tributo a Franco Baresi, pochi minuti prima del fischio d'inizio. Ora l'attenzione della squadra rossonera si sposta sulla 5ª giornata di Europa League, ad Atene contro l'Olympiacos giovedì 26 novembre alle 18.45, per riprendere il discorso nella competizione dopo due sconfitte di fila. Con questa stessa grinta e tanta voglia di far bene. Avanti ragazzi!".

Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon
