Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of today’s Premier League 3pm kick-offs, with Brighton vs Arsenal the pick of the three matches.

Brighton are the league’s top goalscorers so far this season and have amassed the most expected goals, but the champions have the league’s best defence and are seeking five wins from five to start their title defence. There is some welcome needle between Fabian Hurzeler and Mikel Arteta, dating back to Declan Rice’s contentious second yellow for delaying the restart two years ago, as well as the Brighton manager’s comments about Arsenal’s style of play in March.

That 1-0 Arsenal victory at the Amex coincided with Man City dropping points at home to Nottingham Forest on a pivotal night in the title race. Bukayo Saka scored a deflected shot in the ninth minute, and Arsenal held on from there in an ugly but resolute display.

With Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz fit and firing, as well as the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to Arteta’s midfield stable, Arsenal’s football has been more technical and enterprising so far this season. Brighton are one of the few teams who will back themselves to play through Arsenal’s press, which should make for an absorbing game.

It has been revealed that elsewhere, Newcastle are looking to bounce back from their shellacking at Leeds at home to surprise package Hull City. Mattias Jaissle’s team took four points from Liverpool and Spurs but there is concern about how many shots they are conceding. Hull remain unbeaten and continue to confound the odds and underlying data, but that surely cannot last forever.

Everton are also one of the division’s unbeaten teams, but will be targeting three points from a home game against Ipswich after three consecutive draws. Ipswich are sitting comfortably on six points after their win at Crystal Palace, though they did have the extra man for the majority at Selhurst Park.

The second international break of the season is upon us, which is a good time to take stock of how things are going beyond he men’s first team.

It has been revealed that an ownership and management should not just be judged on one area of the club, but rather multiple different departments. The youth sector needs to be developing players in the right way, while the rising prevalence of women’s football gives added impetus to make the Femminile side as competitive as possible.

It has been revealed that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

That being mentioned, can be hard enough keeping up with how the senior team are doing without thinking about the various other sides operating under the Milan umbrella. So, we have provided a summary of how Milan Futuro, Milan Primavera and Milan Women are doing so far in 2026-27.

Industry observers note that it was all change over the summer for the Futuro as they brought in Sergio Navarro as the head coach. The idea was to create some continuity with Ruben Amorim’s more continental style of football, and the pedigree that the Spaniard has suggested it was a positive move.

While not a necessity, the objective for the campaign will no doubt have been set as competing for promotion back to the third tier, which is the level that the project started at prior to the relegation in 2024-25.

Industry observers note that position: It is a case of so far, so good for Navarro’s men. They sit fourth in the standings with 23 points from 11 games, obtained through seven wins, two draws and two losses. They have scored 21 goals (third-most in the league) and allowed 15.

It has been revealed that importantly, the Futuro have a game in hand on the sides above them. If they win it they would go level with Chievo Verona (yes, that Chievo) and Nibbiano & Valtidone who are on 26 points. The former, however, have a 10 better goal difference.

The U23s are part of the Premier League International Cup and they got past Everton 2-1 in the first game, with matches against Stoke later this month and Tottenham in November to come, both away from home.

Sources indicate that high point: On October 18, Milan’s second team went to the current league-leaders Chievo and beat them 2-1, with Bonomi scoring a late winner. That was an early marker of what this team are capable of. A special mention must go to the Premier League Cup win at Goodison Park against Everton, too.

It has been revealed that low point: That aforementioned win in Verona came in the round after Milan had lost 2-1 at home to Rovato Vertovese. They are a side that have only won twice all season and currently occupy the relegation spots, so it was a big blow before a big response.

In a recent development, key players: There have been multiple players that have stood out. Levin Asanji has scored four goals in the league, as has Lorenzo Ossolo. Fabio Pandolfi has been playing a deeper midfield role and looks to have quality well beyond his 18 years of age, with three goals to his name.

Industry observers note that silvano Vos is having a resurgence, while the likes of Emanuele Sala, Mattia Cappelletti, Alessandro Bonomi and Emanuele Borsani have all started every single game, aiding their development under the new coach. El Hadji Malick Cisse – a January arrival – is also turning a lot of heads.

For a bit more deeper reading on the tactical approach used by Milan Futuro under Navarro, we suggest reading the analysis we put out over the international break.

The 2025-26 season was a mixed one for the Primavera side, as their record of 11 wins and 11 defeats in 38 games demonstrates perfectly. They finished 11th, nine points off the relegation play-offs but 10 points off the Scudetto play-offs, though a lot of the younger talents had been again accelerated into the Futuro side.

It has been revealed that giovanni Renna remained at the helm going into the new campaign, the coach that has been promoted up the ranks and thus knows a lot of the players. The hope was that continuity would yield better results, and so far it has.

Position: At the time of writing, the U20 side are sixth in the Primavera 1 league, which puts them in a final play-off spot. They have won five of their first 10 games but they have also lost four, so they remain a bit of a rollercoaster ride of inconsistency.

Looking upwards, Parma are right now top on 21 points, but the Rossoneri are within striking distance of Inter, who are in second on 19 points. However, Renna’s side are also a bad round away from being in the bottom half too.

Recent findings suggest that milan Primavera progressed in the Coppa Italia Primavera at the end of October, beating Catanzaro 2-1 thanks to a late winner from Dotta. Como are the opponents in the next round.

Recent findings suggest that high point: It’s hard to look past the last two rounds in truth. The Primavera seem to have really clicked, scoring 10 goals in the last 180 minutes of action, beating Monza 5-0 away from home and then AlbinoLeffe 5-1 at home.

An honourable mention must go to the 2-0 win over Juventus in September, given they are in a similar position with also having a B-team (Juve Next Gen), so they will continue to serve as a useful point of comparison.

It has been revealed that low point: Back on October 10, the young Diavoli lost 2-0 against Atalanta which was their third league defeat in a row. There was talk of crisis mode as the slide down the table continued, and against an Atalanta side that are now third-bottom of the league. Thankfully, they turned it around swiftly.

Key players: A bit like with the Futuro, the goals have been shared around the Milan Primavera squad. Mattia Zaramella has emerged recently as a star with four goals, as has Max Anastasio who arrived from Bologna and has the same amount.

Industry observers note that then, Andrea Cullotta (a centre-back), Vincent Ibrahimovic (a midfielder) and Edoardo Tartaglia (a full-back) all have two goals. Renna has called upon the same core group of players largely. Matteo Geroli, Francesco Domnitei, Cullotta, Zaramella, Tartaglia, Anastasio and Yanis Massaouadi have all appeared in every round.

Last season was not one that Milan Women will want to shout about, given that they finished sixth in the table and seven points off the play-off spots in the end. They won just nine of 22 games, placing them below even Fiorentina and Lazio, plus Juventus, city rivals Inter and eventual champions Roma.

However, like with the Primavera, consistency was the name of the game. So, Suzanne Bakker remained as the head coach, and there wasn’t as much player turnover as in some recent years.

Position: There have only been seven rounds so far in Serie A Femminile, but the Rossonere have got off to a stuttering start. They have just seven points from their opening seven games, which puts them in eighth place in the table. They have scored 11 goals but let in a joint-league-high 16.

According to recent reports, looking upwards, Roma lead the way with 21 points having won every game. Inter are second on 16 points – so nine more than Milan – while Juventus occupy the final play-off spot on 12. Over their shoulders, Sassuolo are in bottom (the only relegation spot), with three points.

In the Women’s Cup, Milan drew 1-1 with Como, beat Como 1907 (affiliated with the men’s team presently in Serie A, the others are a stand-alone club) 2-1, and then lost 1-0 to Juventus to end their campaign.

High point: This one is quite an easy pick, and it has to be the 2-1 victory over Juventus last month. Thea Kyvåg and Monica Renzotti overturned Lenzini’s opener, which had come with just under a quarter of an hour left on the clock, engineering a late comeback that sparked jubilant scenes.

Sources indicate that low point: The tone for what has been a disappointing campaign so far for Bakker’s ladies was set in round one, when they were beaten 4-1 by Como 1907. Then, losing 1-0 away at Como was another dark day, given they have only won twice.

On November 7, the 3-0 derby defeat to Inter – which included a red card for Milan – served only to highlight the substantial gulf between the two teams at the moment.

Key players: Christy Grimshaw remains the shining light for Milan Women, with three goals and an assist to her name. The scoring charts then see Sara Stokic on three goals, with Sara Fornes, Park Soojeong and Monica Renzotti all netting twice.

Sources indicate that grimshaw is one of three players to start every game so far under Bakker, with the others being defenders Angelica Soffia and Nerea Nevado. Sandra Estevez has emerged as the number one between the sticks too.

Sources indicate that la Juventus ha battuto 4-0 il Venezia, ma nel postpartita di ieri Luciano Spalletti ha svelato il segreto di Pulcinella. Riguarda la costruzione della rosa, le scelte fatte sul mercato e soprattutto la posizione di Randal Kolo Muani. Il francese ha anche ritrovato il gol, ma il suo allenatore non è ancora convinto di come interpreti il ruolo di centravanti. Ed è proprio questo il punto: se Kolo Muani non può essere considerato un vero numero 9, la Juventus rischia di ritrovarsi con un reparto offensivo sovraffollato sugli esterni e con pochissime alternative al centro.

"Quello che mi rode un po' è che ho un sovraccarico sugli esterni e allora provo Kolo Muani a giocare centrale", ha spiegato Spalletti dopo la partita. Una dichiarazione piuttosto significativa, soprattutto se si considera che il francese è stato uno degli investimenti più importanti dell'ultimo mercato bianconero. Il tecnico ha poi chiarito quali siano le difficoltà: "Quando non trova spazio diventa difficile. Spesso ha poca possibilità di spaziare e mettere in moto le qualità se sta fermo. Deve venire più incontro". Non è soltanto una questione di caratteristiche individuali, ma anche di necessità. La Juventus ha già tanti giocatori in grado di agire sulle fasce: quando tornerà ci sarà ovviamente Kenan Yildiz, ma per ora bastano e avanzano Conceiçao, Zhegrova, Boga, Nico Gonzalez e Alajbegovic. Aggiungere anche Kolo Muani all'elenco significherebbe aumentare ulteriormente la concorrenza, senza risolvere il problema del centravanti.

La questione diventa ancora più evidente considerando le alternative a disposizione di Spalletti. Nick Woltemade, decisivo ieri con il suo ingresso dalla panchina, è l'altro attaccante chiamato a occupare il centro dell'area. Poi c'è Jeff Ekhator, appena recuperato e ancora tutto da valorizzare. "Io ho la necessità di avere anche Kolo Muani oltre a Woltemade che giochi in quella posizione lì. Lo dice la composizione della nostra rosa", ha ammesso l'allenatore. Parole che fotografano uno squilibrio del mercato estivo: la Juventus ha investito molto sull'attacco, ma non ha indovinato entrambe le scelte. Ora c'è da operare a gennaio: se si continua a parlare della ricerca di un altro numero 9 - indicato anche dallo stesso allenatore come una necessità -, forse la risposta è già nelle parole di Spalletti.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Taty Castellanos was facing trial by video after being accused of spitting on Filip Marschall during Saturday’s febrile 2-2 draw at the Den.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A spitting row marred the 100th Millwall-West Ham United derby and first for 14 years.

Taty Castellanos was facing trial by video after being accused of spitting on Filip Marschall during Saturday’s febrile 2-2 draw at the Den.

Millwall goalkeeper Marschall made the allegation to referee Paul Tierney, who was expected to include it in an official report that would then be assessed by the Football Association.

Spitting on an opponent is punishable with a six-match ban.

Telegraph Sport has been told West Ham striker Castellanos denies he spat on Marschall and believes he will be vindicated by video footage of the incident.

Lying little prick. Taty didn't spit ❌ pic.twitter.com/5vYxOtKqof.

Millwall manager Alex Neil stated after the game that fourth official Lewis Smith had confirmed a spitting accusation had been made.

Recent findings suggest that asked if he had spoken to Marschall about the claim, Neil replied: “I haven’t asked him about it. But it’s like anything else; I’m sure there’ll be footage of it, or not of it, if it didn’t happen.

Industry observers note that “I’d be extremely surprised if Fil’s made an accusation and nothing’s happened. But that’s not really for me to deal with; I’m sure the authorities will deal with that.”.

Industry observers note that west Ham manager Nuno Espírito Santo said: “I’m aware of the allegation. I didn’t see the image; I didn’t speak with Taty. I cannot go much further on that.”.

He added: “I’m going to try to look at the images.”.

There were also ugly scenes at full time when players had to be separated at the end of a derby that had been at the centre of an unprecedented police operation.

There were six arrests as of 4pm on Saturday for offences including tailgating, assault on a police officer and entering or attempting to enter a stadium while intoxicated.

Eleven men were also arrested at around 7.15pm on Friday on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage.

The group, believed to be Millwall fans, were detained in the vicinity of a known West Ham supporters’ pub in Stratford.

Saturday’s fixture was subject to a five-mile dispersal zone, the largest ever for a football match in London, with officers granted special powers to stop and search people and vehicles without reasonable suspicion and to remove anyone causing disorder.

Riot police were out in force outside the ground, with dog units and mounted officers among 400 personnel deployed – roughly quadruple the usual number for a game there.

Those and other measures – including the use of live facial recognition, a strict segregation policy and a 12.30pm kick-off to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time – prevented a repeat of the kind of violence which has marred this fixture down the years.

West Ham fans also received a police escort to a game that saw both sets of supporters hurl foul-mouthed insults at each other throughout.

Prepares to keep rival spectators apart after the match were reportedly tested by scuffles that broke out as people left the ground.

If the police were ready for a fight before the game, West Ham’s players were not as Millwall tore into them from the first whistle and dominated a first half in which they scored twice through Caleb Taylor and Camiel Neghli and hit the crossbar through a stunning 35-yard strike by Mark Sykes.

This rivalry was forged in different circumstances from most derby confrontations. There is none of the religious divide of Celtic and Rangers, or the politics of Barcelona against Real Madrid, or the spat over title-winning superiority of Manchester United and Liverpool. This is a tale of proximity, an internecine feud.

“There’s no politics, no nationality, nothing like that,” says Nick Hart, who hosts the weekly podcast Achtung! Millwall. “We’re very similar people, from the same backgrounds, same communities. But it’s in the Millwall supporter’s DNA for West Ham to be the ultimate rivals. Nobody else comes into the equation. You’re brought up on this stuff. It’s your history.”.

It has been revealed that though possibly more recent history than might be suggested by the two clubs’ early foundations. The hostility that West Ham will face at the Den is no more about dockland rivalry, north-south London disputes or strike-breaking than the animosity when Manchester United visit Anfield is caused by the building of the Manchester Ship Canal.

“It really is about the hooligan era,” says a podcaster who uses the pseudonym Former West Ham Employee on the West Ham Way podcast. “The two clubs had notorious fanbases. And they grated. It came about through vying to be the No 1, battling to see who had the hardest mob. Whenever we’ve played – or even been in close proximity – things have happened.”.

It has been revealed that jake Cooper on making the 500th appearance of his career against West Ham today! 👏Watch all the action with NOW! https://t.co/56JOZ0NPsr pic.twitter.com/lTzXOwXhxd.

Recent findings suggest that there have only been 18 meetings between these fierce rivals since the Second World War, but absence has certainly not made the heart grow fonder. Here are some of the feud’s most notable flashpoints.

It has been revealed that at the 1972 testimonial in honour of Harry Cripps – the renowned Millwall hard man – police horses were sent on to the pitch after West Ham supporters entered the home section at The Den. Fighting spilt over into the streets surrounding the ground.

An even bleaker turn came in 1976, when Millwall fan Ian Pratt died in a skirmish with West Ham fans at Latest Cross station that led to his fall under a train.

Leaflets were later handed out in the Den’s Cold Blow Lane end with a grainy picture of Pratt and a declaration in capital letters: “A West Ham fan must die next week to avenge him.”.

Millwall plundered four goals on Mothering Sunday in 2004 as Tim Cahill’s double helped them to a 4-1 victory over West Ham at the Den in an incident-filled derby.

Industry observers note that the hosts missed a penalty and had another saved by Stephen Bywater, who was later sent off. Violence followed in the stands and the match was named “The Mothers’ Day Massacre”.

Mother's Day Massacre ⏮️A 4-1 victory over The Hammers back in 2004. pic.twitter.com/TLi7xkcVJG.

A hundred West Ham and Millwall supporters clashed during a screening of England’s 2006 World Cup match against Paraguay in Canada Square, which led to 16 injuries and one hospitalisation.

The clubs’ League Cup meeting in 2009 at Upton Park was listed as Category Five by police, the most serious risk of violence, and resulted in a Millwall supporter being stabbed in Priory Road, near the ground.

The Metropolitan Police remarked that “planned” scuffles, which involved more than 100 fans, appeared to have been caused by fans without tickets to the game.

Industry observers note that just spotted one Millwall fan outside the ground in blue boxing gloves. He is also wearing what appear to be slippers, so not sure what that means….

Nuno Espirito Santo has only been through the door at West Ham for a matter of months, but he insisted he is fully aware of the significance of today’s fixture.

When asked about his perception of the rivalry, Nuno said: “Since the fixture list came out, this date has been [important], for both of the clubs. It’s special, special game. We look forward to go and compete against a good team.

“It’s a different game from all of the other games, it’s a special game, the atmosphere will be different… Steve [Potts, first-team coach and former West Ham player] has been involved in many of these games, he’s constantly speaking about how special it is for West Ham fans, so we have a lot of information and we are fully aware of the importance of the game.

On potential unrest between fans and the significant police presence, Nuno added: “What we want most is that everything goes well, both fans supporting their teams and no conflict. We have people inside the club who are taking care of that. We have to focus on our tasks.”.

The gaffer on tomorrow's fixture ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/6NG6t4t4Fn.

According to recent reports, riot police are very much out in force outside The Den today for the 100th competitive derby between Millwall and West Ham United and first for 14 years. Dog units and mounted officers can been seen patrolling the perimeter of the ground, with 400 personnel deployed to stop violence erupting between rival fans – roughly quadruple the usual number for a fixture here. There has been no sign of any trouble with less than an hour to go before kick-off.

In a recent development, the game has been scheduled for 12.30pm to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time, although plenty of fans have been nursing pints before entering the ground. Other measures in place include the use of live facial recognition cameras, while a dispersal order has been imposed covering a large area around the stadium. Police were also planning to escort West Ham fans from South Bermondsey station, which will also be closed to home supporters for up to an hour after full-time. The latter measure has been deemed safer than holding the 1,800 away fans back following the game.

The Millwall-West Ham derby is one of the most notorious in English football and was most recently marred by serious violence when the sides met at Upton Park for a League Cup tie back in 2009. One man was stabbed and the match itself was interrupted on three occasions by fans invading the pitch.

The Metropolitan Police will have 400 officers on the streets of east London for this match – about four times the norm for a Championship fixture – and it has enforced a Section 35 dispersal order in the area highlighted on the map below.

A Section 35 order authorises a Police Constable and a Police Community Support Officer in uniform to “exclude a person from an area for a period of up to 48 hours with an Inspector’s authority”.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of the highly anticipated Championship match between Millwall and West Ham United as the two clubs meet officially for the 100th time. This fixture has not been staged since 2012, and the intervening 14 years have done little to temper the ill-feeling between their passionate supporters, who will be anxious to claim bragging rights over their Dockers Derby rivals. The Metropolitan Police have placed a Section 35 dispersal order in the area surrounding The Den and will deploy 400 officers on the streets of east London.

Recent findings suggest that acrimony between the two clubs has existed since the late 19th century when Millwall Athletic, originally Rovers, battled it out against Thames Ironworks, later renamed West Ham at the Athletic and Memorial Grounds. Sixty of the two clubs’ 99 meetings came between 1899 and 1915, and while they played just seven times between 1946 and 1987, the irregularity of the game only added to its mystique, which has often spilt over into the ugly.

According to recent reports, both head coaches spoke at length about the significance of today’s match, with Alex Neil, in the Millwall dugout, describing it as an encounter that means “absolutely everything” but imploring his players to keep “cool heads”. His counterpart Nuno Espírito Santo revealed that he had been well advised about the game’s importance by Steve Potts, his first-team coach and former West Ham player.

Since the club’s last meeting in 2012, West Ham have ascended into the Premier League, moved into the London Stadium and won the Uefa Conference League, only falling back into England’s second tier last summer where Millwall have remained for all but two seasons. The Lions brushed maddeningly close to promotion in their last campaign as they pushed for an automatic spot until the very last weekend of the regular season before falling to Hull City in the play-off semi-finals.

Sources indicate that much of the pre-match talk will centre on the clubs’ long-standing rivalry, but beneath the bile and belligerence is an intriguing football match between two sides. Millwall are missing 11 first-team players and face the daunting task of stopping a West Ham side who have found their feet in the Championship, scoring 16 goals in their last four league matches.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Blackburn Rovers face Burnley in a Lancashire derby on Sunday.
  • Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds will lead the side on an interim basis, but the temporary bosses will not be able to call upon star right-back Ryan Alebiosu.
  • Industry observers note that summer signing Gady Beyuku replaced Alebiosu when he hobbled off against Stoke City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blackburn Rovers face Burnley in a Lancashire derby on Sunday. It’s a substantial occasion at Ewood Park, not only because of the rivalry, but because it marks Rovers’ first game since Tony Mowbray stepped back as head coach due to health issues earlier this week.

Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds will lead the side on an interim basis, but the temporary bosses will not be able to call upon star right-back Ryan Alebiosu. The Nigerian international has undergone surgery on his knee and is set to be sidelined until the Upcoming Year.

Industry observers note that summer signing Gady Beyuku replaced Alebiosu when he hobbled off against Stoke City. And, he played the full 90 minutes against West Ham while the medical staff waited for a verdict on Alebiosu’s blow.

Now that we know how long Blackburn Rovers’ go-to right-back will be out for, Beyuku has a real chance to make the starting role his own.

Industry observers note that most clubs have at least two players to cover in every position, and that is the case at Blackburn Rovers. With Alebiosu out, Beyuku is the only natural senior right-back available for selection, paving the way for him to come into the side.

Industry observers note that A reported fee of around £1.2m was paid to sign the 20-year-old from Modena in the summer, so there is clear belief in his potential. It was widely expected that Beyuku would be cover and competition for Alebiosu, but the injury thrusts him into the limelight.

Recent findings suggest that he’s shown signs of growing into Championship football early on as well. His second-half against West Ham was the best we’ve seen from Beyuku to date, offering a lively presence up and down the right-hand side.

The Frenchman saw to his duties at the back with 10 defensive contributions, but he was forward-thinking and frequently involved in possession like Alebiosu as well. Beyuku completed 26 of his 29 passes, nine of which were line-breaking.

He was dispossessed twice, but this does come with the territory of being a progressive right-back who is still developing and settling into a new league (all stats via FotMob).

In a recent development, alebiosu’s shoes are major ones to fill. It might not have been planned that Beyuku would assume a starting role this early into his Blackburn Rovers, given his age and need to grow into Championship football.

It means that, despite the fact he needs to deliver, there should be an element of patience.

Recent findings suggest that if Johnson and Dodds feel Beyuku needs to be taken out of the side, there are options to consider. Kristi Montgomery has a key role in midfield alongside Sam Morsy but he has covered at right-back before. Matty Litherland is working his way back from injury too, while Lewis Miller is a longer-term absentee.

Beyuku will have the firm backing of the Rovers faithful. A strong display against arch-rivals Burnley this Sunday would be a sure-fire way for the youngster to endear himself to the fans and announce himself in Championship football.

Il Milan ha vinto 5-1 contro il Frosinone, ma, a fine partita, le dichiarazioni di Gerry Cardinale e di Ruben Amorim sono state - apparentemente - differenti per quanto riguarda il percorso della squadra.

"Siamo a novembre. Abbiamo ancora molta strada da fare. Ma in ogni partita vogliamo vedere dei miglioramenti. Questo weekend è stato molto interessante se guardi il tipo di risultati che ci sono stati. Si può vedere che qualcosa sta cambiando in Serie A. Sono stato molto contento di vederci non solo vincere, ma vincere con quel margine. E, quindi, dobbiamo costruirci sopra, ma come dice Amorim, ogni partita è qualcosa su cui costruire e abbiamo molta strada da fare. Io personalmente mi aspetto ancora che competiamo per lo scudetto, ma è lontano. Una partita alla volta. Ora l'attenzione è sull'Europa League. Sì, e come ha detto Ruben dobbiamo fare entrambe le cose. Le competizioni europee sono importanti. Tutto è un banco di prova. Se vuoi vincere uno scudetto, devi farlo fino in fondo, ed è quello che faremo".

Quello che ho percepito contro il Genoa e nelle altre partite è che eravamo troppo lontani, non arrivavamo nell'ultimo terzo di campo. Non siamo come le significant: se guardate le grandi squadre, per esempio la Juventus, magari fatica nei risultati, ma vedete il volume che produce. Per noi è un po' l'opposto, quindi sono davvero preoccupato che, se non miglioriamo, non potremo mantenere questo numero di punti. Oggi però è stato un passo avanti: si sono visti tanti giocatori attaccare la profondità, cosa che non si era vista contro il Ferencvaros. Nelle altre gare avevamo gestito bene il pallone, ma oggi servivano ritmo e corse. Dobbiamo riuscire a giocare entrambe le partite all'interno della stessa gara, ma oggi era chiaramente il tipo di partita che dovevamo fare per vincere".

Recent findings suggest that la squadra di Ignazio Abate affronta la capolista guidata da Gennaro Gattuso dopo essere scivolata al tredicesimo posto. I granata hanno raccolto appena un punto nelle ultime quattro giornate, dopo una serie di tre vittorie consecutive a ottobre. Per il tecnico, al debutto in Serie A, la partita rappresenta un’occasione per invertire la rotta.

La Stampa presenta così il momento del tecnico e la sfida di sabato: «Toro, tutti i dolori del giovane Abate: serve coraggio per uscire dalla crisi. Il tecnico chiamato a rialzare la squadra: sabato con la capolista Lazio si gioca la grande chance».

According to recent reports, il quotidiano richiama le difficoltà nella costruzione del gioco: 15 gol segnati in 12 giornate. Servirà il contributo dei senatori come Simeone, Adams e Vlasic e la stessa determinazione mostrata da Lucas Perri, capace di riscattarsi dopo un avvio difficile fino a fare la differenza al Maradona».

La Lazio è allenata da Gattuso, che in passato era stato cercato dallo stesso Cairo.

Sources indicate that L’esclusione di Rodriguez dalla trasferta partenopea è legata a una vicenda disciplinare. Il difensore, reduce da una lesione tendinea, non avrebbe mantenuto la promessa di curarsi al Filadelfia durante la sosta, scegliendo invece di rispondere alla convocazione della Svizzera.

La Stampa ricostruisce così la decisione del club: «Il Toro punisce Rodriguez: una lezione per lo spogliatoio. Il difensore svizzero non è rimasto a Torino per problemi fisici, bensì per scelta della società dopo non aver mantenuto la promessa di curarsi al Filadelfia durante la sosta. Pur reduce da una lesione tendinea, Rodriguez ha preferito rispondere alla chiamata della Svizzera per tagliare il traguardo delle 150 presenze contro la Scozia, scatenando il confronto con il ds Petrachi e lo stop punitivo».

In a recent development, chissà se questa sera Eddy Kouadio indosserà, metaforicamente parlando, il suo vestito migliore. Alle 20:45, nella sfida del Brianteo contro la Fiorentina, il giovane difensore del Monza si troverà infatti di fronte al suo passato e (forse) al suo futuro. Il classe 2006, infatti, è ancora di proprietà del club viola, che sta osservando con grande soddisfazione la sua crescita, maturata anche grazie alla sapiente guida di Ivan Juric. Una serata, dunque, in cui Kouadio avrà l'occasione di mettersi in mostra proprio davanti a chi, per primo, ha creduto nel suo talento.

Kouadio, nato a Prato, è cresciuto nelle giovanili viola dove vi milita dal 2021. Il ragazzo si è messo in mostra al grande pubblico per la prima volta la scorsa stagione, giocata tra prima squadra e Primavera. Con i grandi Kouadio ha messo a referto cinque presenze in Conference League a cui se ne sommano altre tre in Serie A. Nella Primavera di Galloppa, invece, il difensore ci ha giocato poco ma è stato comunque determinante nella vittoria dello Scudetto realizzando pure il gol decisivo nella finale vinta 2-1 contro il Parma. Il giocatore resta legato alla Fiorentina da un contratto fino al 2030 e in estate farà certamente ritorno al Viola Park, vedremo se per restare o se per salutare di nuovo, magari questa volta in modo definitivo.

Il presente, però, si chiama Monza. E questa sera Kouadio sarà chiamato a fare la sua parte per evitare il quinto ko consecutivo, un risultato che rischierebbe di compromettere quanto di buono costruito dai brianzoli nella prima parte di stagione. Toccherà ancora a lui presidiare il centro-destra della retroguardia disegnata da Juric, che considera il classe 2006 un punto fermo del proprio scacchiere tattico. I numeri, del resto, raccontano meglio di qualsiasi parola il suo peso nella squadra visto che Kouadio è partito titolare in nove delle dieci gare fin qui disputate, diventando il secondo giocatore della rosa per minutaggio, alle spalle del solo Birindelli. Prestazioni e continuità che non sono passate inosservate, attirando non soltanto l'attenzione della Fiorentina, ma anche quella del CT Roberto Mancini, che lo scorso settembre gli ha già aperto le porte della Nazionale maggiore con una prima convocazione, in attesa di poter festeggiare anche il debutto.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leicester City are eyeing an immediate promotion back from League One to the Championship this season under the guidance of head coach Russell Martin. LCFC slipped out of the second tier earlier this year after they finished in the bottom three along with Sheffield Wednesday and Oxford United.

It has been revealed that the Foxes should target a move for Hull City attacking midfielder Kieran Dowell this winter to boost their chances of going up. The Merseyside-born man is expected to leave the Tigers after being left out of their 25-man squad in the Premier League.

Dowell, 29, has played only once for the East Yorkshire outfit in the Carabao Cup so far in this campaign and a change of scene will do him good. He is out of contract at the MKM Stadium in June next year after they handed him an 18-month deal last January when he signed.

Dowell would give Leicester City more competition and depth in their attacking department. He could also inject more quality into LCFC’s squad.

He played with Foxes’ midfielder John Lundstram at Hull City last term. The pair helped the Tigers win the play-offs and reach the top flight against the odds.

Dowell’s game time has dried up under Sergej Jakirovic since then though and he is now surplus to requirements. He was offered to Sheffield United in the summer but nothing materialised on that front in the end and he stayed put beyond the last deadline.

In a recent development, the ex-England youth international is available now though and landing him would be a statement of intent by Leicester City if they managed to get him. He will surely have interest from the division above but the prospect of regular minutes could turn his head.

Dowell had a spell in League One with Birmingham City in 2025. He helped the Blues win the title under Chris Davies.

In a recent development, therefore, he knows what it takes to get out of Leicester City’s league. His experience would come in very handy for LCFC and he would be a useful character to have in and around the dressing room.

It has been revealed that dowell rose up through Everton’s academy as a youngster. He has also had stints at Sheffield United, Derby County, Norwich City, Wigan Athletic, Norwich City and Rangers.

A deal wouldn’t break the bank, and it could give Russell Martin a valuable extra creative spark.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mattinata di tensione sull'autostrada A1 per i tifosi del Torino, protagonisti di alcuni scontri con un gruppo di ultras della Roma.
  • According to recent reports, I sostenitori granata erano in viaggio verso Napoli, dove alle 20.45 la squadra di Ignazio Abate era attesa dalla sfida contro i partenopei al 'Maradona'.
  • L'episodio assume un significato particolare anche per il momento in cui si è verificato.

Mattinata di tensione sull'autostrada A1 per i tifosi del Torino, protagonisti di alcuni scontri con un gruppo di ultras della Roma. L'episodio, riportato da Tuttosport, si è verificato nella mattinata di sabato, nei pressi dell'area di servizio Arno Est, in prossimità di Firenze, dove le due tifoserie si sono incrociate mentre erano entrambe dirette verso i rispettivi impegni di campionato.

According to recent reports, I sostenitori granata erano in viaggio verso Napoli, dove alle 20.45 la squadra di Ignazio Abate era attesa dalla sfida contro i partenopei al 'Maradona'. I tifosi giallorossi, invece, stavano raggiungendo Parma per assistere alla partita del Tardini, in programma alle 18. L'incontro tra i due gruppi sarebbe rapidamente degenerato, dando origine a momenti di tensione e a veri e propri scontri. Secondo quanto ricostruito, alcuni van utilizzati dai sostenitori del Torino avrebbero riportato danni, mentre diversi tifosi granata avrebbero avuto bisogno di cure in ospedale. Non si registrerebbero, tuttavia, feriti in gravi condizioni.

L'episodio assume un significato particolare anche per il momento in cui si è verificato. La trasferta di Napoli rappresentava infatti la prima occasione stagionale nella quale tutti i tifosi del Torino, compresi quelli residenti nel capoluogo piemontese e nella relativa provincia, potevano seguire liberamente la squadra lontano dallo stadio Olimpico Grande Torino. Una possibilità rimasta preclusa fino a questo momento in seguito al provvedimento del Viminale dello scorso giugno, adottato dopo i noti episodi di violenza verificatisi prima del derby contro la Juventus.

Breaking: 3 left-backs West Ham must eye as after Scott Parker makes January transfer demands

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (622 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Ham must first navigate a busy December schedule before the January transfer window opens, but Scott Parker is already planning to strengthen his squad.
  • Industry observers note that the left-back role has been an issue for WHU this season after the departure of El Hadji Malick Diouf.
  • Adama Boiro was brought in late in the summer window but he has managed just 13 minutes of league action since his arrival.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham must first navigate a busy December schedule before the January transfer window opens, but Scott Parker is already planning to strengthen his squad. The Hammers boss has identified two key positions he wants to address, with a new striker and left-back both on his January wish list.

Industry observers note that the left-back role has been an issue for WHU this season after the departure of El Hadji Malick Diouf. Academy duo Ezra Mayers and Ollie Scarles have had opportunities in that role but have failed to nail down the spot.

Adama Boiro was brought in late in the summer window but he has managed just 13 minutes of league action since his arrival. There only other option in that role has been Morato but he is a natural centre-back.

With that said, here are three left-backs that could solve Scott Parker’s complications at West Ham….

In a recent development, harrison Burrows brings a different, more attacking dimension from left-back. At Sheffield United he has posted strong goal and assist numbers while operating as a left-back or wing-back, showing he can contribute in the final third as well as defend.

Sources indicate that that end product is useful for a West Ham side that needs more threat from deeper areas. Energetic in the press and capable of overlapping or underlapping, he adds balance to a back line that has often lacked a specialist left-sided option.

In a recent development, while he has no prior Parker connection, his Championship pedigree and creative output make him a sensible complementary target alongside more defensively oriented options. He would give Parker a player who can both protect and progress.

Lucas Pires stands out because of his direct experience under Parker. During Burnley’s 2024/25 Championship promotion campaign he was a regular starter at left-back, logging a high number of appearances in a side that prioritised defensive organisation and controlled possession.

That familiarity with Parker’s demands is valuable for West Ham, who are still bedding in a new system. At Championship level he has shown reliability in one-v-one defending, solid positioning and the ability to recycle possession calmly.

In a recent development, still only in his mid-twenties and currently at Burnley, he represents a realistic, modest-fee option rather than a high-risk gamble. His prior success in Parker’s set-up reduces the adaptation period and gives West Ham a proven, system-ready left-back who has already contributed to a promotion.

Harry Amass offers a high-upside profile that fits a promotion-chasing side. At 19 he has already accumulated meaningful Championship minutes on loan at Sheffield Wednesday and Norwich City, demonstrating he can handle the physical and technical demands of the division.

Athletic, left-footed and comfortable stepping into midfield, he provides both defensive cover and progressive carrying from the back. Limited first-team opportunities at Manchester United make a permanent or long-term move plausible, and he has been repeatedly linked with West Ham.

For Parker, Amass represents a younger, more dynamic alternative who can grow into the role over multiple seasons while still delivering immediate Championship quality. His age, athletic traits and proven second-tier experience make him an attractive, future-proof target.

#72711. All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

📅 20 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 30m • 📚 Deep Dive (5900 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

📅 20 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 30 min read (5900 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~30 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that for all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper.
  • Industry observers note that we keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing?
  • Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that for all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper. And it is already costing them dear.

Industry observers note that we keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing? Maybe not since his Bournemouth days.

Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.

It is a puzzle how Tottenham signed 10 fresh players, but did not upgrade two of the most notable positions on the pitch.

Only when Aston Villa were out of sight and the game was effectively over did Spurs break their Premier League goal drought. And even then it was a midfielder, Conor Gallagher, and a defender, Jan Paul van Hecke, who were on target.

Solanke had gone off just before Villa scored their second goal, which highlighted the substantial difference between the two sides on Saturday and where Spurs are badly lacking.

It has been revealed that zion Suzuki, the Villa goalkeeper, released a long ball upfield, Nicolas Jackson managed to lay it off for Johan Mazambi, who returned the favour. Jackson touched the ball past Micky van de Ven’s challenge before beating Kinsky with a well-struck shot.

Spurs are stunned as Nicolas Jackson doubles Aston Villa's lead 😳📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/il7NKbgFCQ.

Recent findings suggest that it was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

Industry observers note that spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Recent findings suggest that asked if Tottenham had made a big mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi said: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

Recent findings suggest that “We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”.

That sounded a bit like excuses, but De Zerbi did not put up much of a defence for Solanke as he remarked: “We need more from him, for sure, but he’s one of my players. I like Dom as a player and I stay with him until the end. He needs to stay better, to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough, but it’s normal for him. Maybe he is not confident enough in himself at this moment, because he’s much better than this. I think we can’t say everything is bad, but it’s not enough.”.

In a recent development, it was Sávio who forced Suzuki into making a brilliant double save from him in the first half, when Tottenham were well on top. The Japan international also stopped an Archie Gray shot from squirming through his legs and into the net, and dived to turn another Sávio effort around his right-hand post.

Industry observers note that jackson was not the only Villa new boy who upstaged Tottenham’s expensive new attackers. Manzambi not only assisted for Jackson, but also marked his first start for the Midlands club with a goal that put the visitors ahead in first-half stoppage time.

Johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm.

Andrew Robertson will have been disappointed with his attempt to clear the ball, John McGinn played it into the path of Boubacar Kamara and his scuffed shot fell into the path of Manzambi, who found the back of the net.

Substitute Mohammed Kudus was correctly denied an equaliser following a VAR check before Jackson’s goal and a brilliant strike from Emiliano Buendía that effectively clinched a first league win of the season for Villa.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Unai Emery, the head coach, spent years watching Martínez and Ollie Watkins win games for Villa with decisive actions, and is hoping this was evidence that Suzuki and Jackson can do the same for him.

“They are here for it [making the same impact],” Emery said. “His commitment, Zion is really very good. His commitment, Nico Jackson as well is fantastic. But every player needs to understand how we can feel better collectively, how they can help us with their qualities, and how we can collectively exploit our best performance.

“Today we made one clear step forward. Zion is keeping his performance like he did before. Jackson today clearly improved his performance. This is the way forward and the example for the other players.

“Manzambi played a good match, but he’s not yet understanding everything we need on the field with our positioning. He’s a fantastic player and must feel free playing to try to exploit himself and his qualities. But, of course, always under our structure.”.

Speaking after the match, former Spurs man Joe Cole was critical of the club’s summer business which has left them without an out-and-out goalscorer and a weak defence.

"You can't rule them out of a relegation battle"Steven Gerrard and Joe Cole have major concerns for Spurs 😬🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/JivM5pNfM9.

Plenty of fans leaving before full-time...

and heartbreak for the ones that stayed...

"It's a long international break, you don't want to be in the bottom three"John McGinn on the 'relief' for Aston Villa to pick up their first league win of the season 😅🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Gl38uj1pig.

We’ve got a three-week international break after this weekend, so there’s a little while before both teams will be back in action, but this is what awaits them when they return:.

vs Man Utd (A) - Oct 10th, 5.30pm.

vs Coventry (H) - Oct 19th, 8pm.

vs Chelsea (A) - Oct 24th, 5.30pm.

vs Crystal Palace (H) - Oct 31st, 5.30pm.

vs Brentford (H) - Oct 10th, 3pm.

vs Fenerbahce (H) - Oct 14th, 8pm.

vs Newcastle (A) - Oct 17th, 5.30pm.

vs Man City (H) - Oct 24th, 12.30pm.

"The fans deserved the win." 👏Emi Buendia shows his appreciation to Aston Villa supporters after a much-needed victory 💜🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Qjn6RihNGD.

John McGinn is also speaking to TNT now, so we’ll get you his quotes soon.

Villa only had seven touches in the Spurs box in that second half, but that was enough to secure two goals and all three points.

Spurs thought they had pulled themselves level while Villa were only 0-1 up after 60 minutes, but VAR judged Robertson to be offside.

Spurs thought they had their first Premier League goal of the season...Until VAR ruled it out for offside 😬 pic.twitter.com/FJsrLhm0FG.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Possession: Spurs 64% vs 36% Villa.

Touches inside opposition box: 31 vs 18.

Aston Villa have jumped with their first win of the season, while Tottenham have sunk back into the relegation zone.

“We were looking for this win from the beginning. We had a really difficult start of the season in terms of results and not finding our best football but I think today we demonstrated a really good character.”.

In a recent development, and that is it! A second late consolation goal is not enough to stem the boos from the stands.

It has been revealed that late action from Tottenham but they leave it too late to get a result. Another loss at home sends De Zerbi back to the drawing board.

According to recent reports, this will be the last of the game probably as Maddison is fouled outside the area for Spurs’ third free kick in quick succession. Robertson takes it and sends a perfect delivery to the back post.

It is the first one that Mings has been caught under and van Hecke gets there to send it past Suzuki.

Another foul for Spurs, on the corner of the box. Maddison to take again and Mings does great work to judge the path of the ball and head it out from the centre of the box.

Callagher gets the ball in midfield and feeds Savio on the left who pulls it back. The ball he sends into the box is cleared from a crowd of bodies by Barkley.

According to recent reports, though Savio takes the corner rapidly, it comes out to the edge of the area. Bentancur rises to meet the ball lifted in to the box and flicks it on behind himself towards goal, and it just goes wide of the post.

Maddison stands over it, and goes for goal, curling it very well, though Suzuki is in the right place to punch it away. It falls to Kudus, whose follow-up is a much less exciting effort, sailing over the bar.

We will have seven minutes added on here.

Kudus has been fouled as he try to get forward. Spurs are still looking for a second goal and Savio is fouled on the left side of the box. Cash gets a card for it and it is a very interesting position, not far from the touchline.

It has been given as a Gallagher goal for now.

Sources indicate that but it is just too little too late for Spurs. No celebration from De Zerbi and hardly a cheer from the fans remaining in the stadium.

Tammy Abraham has come on by the way, replacing Jackson for the final few minutes.

Recent findings suggest that A consolation for Spurs! They have their first league goal to almost no reaction from their fans.

Kudus cuts the ball back and it is not clear whether Cash or Gallagher get there first to poke it home.

It looks like a Cash own goal...

Sources indicate that the Spurs fans are leaving in droves. All you can hear in the stadium now are the rejoicing Villa fans.

McGinn comes off for Ross Barkley and Kamara off for Mbaye.

Spurs replace Bentancur and Tonali with Lucas Bergvall and Connor Gallagher.

This is absolutely what Villa needed. They have been great out of possession, just patient and disciplined and taking their chances when they come.

This is going to be a long three weeks for De Zerbi. Spurs have not managed a shot on target in the half, despite all their dominance on the ball.

That must be the final nail in the coffin for Spurs.

In a recent development, gomes makes a great run, sending the ball out to McGinn on the right win. Rather than send the ball in to the box, he sends it out to the edge of the area and there is Buendia. He runs on to it late, finding the top left corner with an immaculate strike.

The Spurs fans are flooding out.

According to recent reports, villa have been calm without the ball in this half. Spurs have dominated possession but Villa have been very organised in defence.

Recent findings suggest that gray is fouled 35 yards out and Maddison takes the free kick. It only meets the first man in the box, who is Ruggeri, who clears.

Spurs are having no luck and have just not been able to get themselves in front.

Sources indicate that marmoush gets the ball from Maddison on the edge of the area and takes a shot on the turn. It’s blocked by Lindelof for a corner.

Savio takes again but Suzuki punches it away in the centre of the box.

Kudus tries a ball from on the right of the area, looking to find Robertson at the back post but Suzuki again comes confidently to claim it.

Change for Villa as Manzambi comes off to make way for George Hemmings.

17 minutes for Spurs to find a goal...or two.

In a recent development, tonali comes close! From 35 yards out, the Italian takes a touch to shift it onto his left foot and sends a curling effort towards goal. Suzuki dives but can’t get there and the ball just whistles past the top far corner of the goal.

At least Spurs’s heads haven’t gone down but they still have nothing to show for it.

According to recent reports, savio sends a cross in from the right but there’s only Buendia in the box to meet it. He sends it out and Jackson finds himself with it again on the left side. Villa’s play breaks down but they are not backing down.

Well it’s gone from bad to worse for Spurs.

Jackson gets his first goal for his latest club and van Hecke has got to do better there.

Recent findings suggest that he gets on the end of an incredible long ball from Suzuki, and van Hecke does not get close enough to challenge him. He takes a touch to get it past van de Ven and sends it past Kinsky from the edge of the box into the bottom corner. The keeper gets a hand on it but it comes in off the post, almost in slow motion.

James Maddison will be coming on shortly.

Tonali sends a ball across to Savio on the right corner of the box, and his low ball in goes out the back for a corner.

Solanke can’t control it as it comes in and that will be his last action before he makes way for Maddison.

Marmoush goes down on the edge of the box, pushed by Joao Gomes, earning a free kick.

Recent findings suggest that robertson and Marmoush standing over it, just on the left of the area. Robertson is the one to take, lifting it towards the back post but Suzuki comes out to claim easily.

Industry observers note that so close for Spurs! A fantastic run from Robertson but the defender strays just offside just outside the box. He takes the ball down to the back line, drawing Suzuki off his line, and it is crossed back past the keeper and bundled over the line by Kudus.

Industry observers note that huge cheers before VAR takes a look. The wait goes on.

Ruggeri intercepts a loose ball in midfield and makes a run down the left side. He lifts a ball towards the centre of the box, but Betancur beats the waiting Manzambi to it, bringing it down and nudging it towards his keeper.

Savio again on the right edge of the box lifts a ball across the box towards the back post, but Suzuki judges it well and comes off his line to claim it.

We’re back underway as Kinsky had to receive a bit of treatment there.

It has been revealed that good afternoon and welcome to our coverage of today’s bottom-of-the-table epic: Tottenham Hotspur vs Aston Villa. This tie is incidentally the match-up between the last two winners of the Europa League, though so far neither of them have looked like European champions.

It is definitely fair to say that this season has not started the way either of these teams would have wanted, as the host side currently sit in what is apparently their favourite position – 17th – and the visitors are all the way in 19th, only above Coventry.

Despite getting off to a fairly convincing start in the Champions League with a 3-2 win over Club Brugge, Villa only scored their first league goal last week in their match against Nottingham Forest, though it was a futile one as they still lost 2-1 at Villa Park.

Industry observers note that tottenham meanwhile are still waiting for their first league goal, despite putting one past Liverpool in their 3-1 defeat in the Carabao Cup third round. With no European football and already out of one cup competition, Roberto De Zerbi has only the FA Cup in January and the rest of the league season to drag Spurs out of the perpetual rut they appear to find themselves in. They sit only one point above Villa as they have been able to see out two 0-0 draws – against Everton and Nottingham Forest – instead of one.

There has been plenty of talk about the money spent by both teams, without the results yet to show for it. The total sits around half a billion between them, adding to the mounting pressure on both De Zerbi and Unai Emery. Summer signings for both teams have struggled to land, something which will not be helped by the upcoming international break.

According to recent reports, but before then, the teams have 90 minutes to try and get their seasons up and running, and we will be bringing you the team news, lineups and all the action from the match! Stay tuned!

AC Milan could launch a bid to sign Gabriele Calvani next year, with the young Italian coming into his own in Serie A.

Whilst Milan are becoming more comfortable with buying experienced options, Gerry Cardinale will not abandon the future. So, they’ll continue to try to buy the right players for the future where the opportunity to do so is right; for example, with Sankhoun Diawara.

Gazzetta dello Sport states that Goncalo Inacio is an ‘of course’ option, whilst Virgil van Dijk sits as a ‘why not’. For Calvani, though, the reasoning is more in-depth. He’s not up to the level of his European counterparts just yet, but a promising Italian is something in its own right.

He’s blossomed this year with Frosinone, playing on the right in a 4-2-3-1 set-up. So, there’d be a potential spot for him to replace Fikayo Tomori if he were to depart next year. However, they’d have to deal with Genoa, who are his parent club.

Now could be the perfect time to introduce him to San Siro, allowing him to develop in his own time without needing to push him. For his first season in Serie A, he’s taking to it brilliantly from his pressing to his aerial ability.

They’ll hope to be able to watch him at San Siro this weekend, but it’s tough to know if they’ll be able to, given he’s struggling with a flexor glitch currently. Nevertheless, he’s a concrete target; practical and with potential for the future.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, una prestazione che vale più di una vittoria. Già, perché certe volte le reazioni valgono di più rispetto a quello che si segna sul tabellino. Anzi, forse certi punteggi che magari lasciano un po’ quel “rammarico” o che comunque non sono esenti da errori, però scatenano tutte quelle componenti che richiamano alla consapevolezza di migliorare e di vedere la luce in fondo al tunnel.

Contro l’Inter in un 4-4 spettacolare, l’Atalanta sforna una prestazione coerente con quello che è il suo DNA (che si era visto solo in certi singoli): prima cade, poi risale, poi ricade ancora e si risolleva nel finale nella gioia di tutti. Il tutto all’insegna di una parola tanto semplice quanto grande: squadra.

Dalla prospettiva bergamasca sarebbe facile soffermarsi sull’impronta decisiva dei singoli: la doppietta straordinaria di De Ketelaere, la qualità del trio Zalewski-Rowe-Elmas, la solidità ed esperienza di Mario Pasalic oppure il ritorno del “presidente” Franck Kessié. Tutto importante, certo, ma non quanto lo sia l’intero collettivo. Tutti si sono trascinati a vicenda per cercare un pareggio che, dopo il 2-4 interista, era veramente un’impresa impossibile da centrare, se non con l’unione di tutti. Il giocatore che carica il compagno indipendentemente dal fatto che sbagli un passaggio o faccia una buona azione, l’intesa nel farsi trovare al posto giusto al momento giusto, l’aggredire il portatore di palla con tutte le forze, le pedine offensive che si sporcano le mani in fase difensiva. Elementi che fanno la differenza, senza dimenticare mister Sarri fino ai cambi che non risparmiano neanche una goccia di sudore.

Tante volte in questa stagione si è parlato di un’Atalanta opaca o addirittura poco coerente con ciò che serviva veramente all’interno del rettangolo verde. Una situazione nella quale le critiche e certi fischi potevano servire a far scattare qualcosa, un po’ come un genitore che deve rimproverare il figlio perché va male a scuola. La reazione della squadra, la voglia addirittura di vincerla nel finale, l’esultanza del pubblico, con tutta la squadra che si ferma sotto la Curva Pisani a cantare il coro “Bergamo!” tutta insieme, nessuno escluso: l’unione che fa la forza.

Le grandi imprese non si fanno in un giorno. È il punto di partenza per un nuovo inizio, ma solo se si fa tesoro di quello che è stato fatto ieri sera. Occorre continuità, un filotto per risollevare l’intera china dove ora non bisogna più sbagliare tra campionato e Conference. Una grande speranza, dove tutto dipenderà solo e soltanto dall’Atalanta che, finalmente, ritorna a incarnare l’ABC dei valori lavorativi del bergamasco. Ora non resta che andare avanti.

Il Sassuolo ha perso anche al debutto di Roberto D'Aversa, portando a sei le sconfitte consecutive in Serie A. Il problema, semmai, è che la prima partita della nuova gestione ha mostrato parecchi dei difetti della precedente.

In a recent development, il Sassuolo resta a 8 punti dopo 12 giornate, con appena due vittorie, due pareggi e otto sconfitte. I gol segnati sono 16, quelli subiti addirittura 31, per una differenza reti di -15. La posizione è la diciassettesima, in attesa di Monza-Fiorentina di questa sera, con i brianzoli a quota 7 prima del loro match. La statistica che testimonia meglio la crisi però arriva dalla fase difensiva. Nelle sei sconfitte consecutive il Sassuolo ha incassato 21 reti: quattro dal Frosinone, due dal Como, sei dalla Lazio, quattro dalla Fiorentina, tre dalla Roma e altre due dal Genoa. Tre gol e mezzo subiti di media a partita. Troppi per pensare che basti cambiare sistema o aggiustare qualche distanza. Contro il Genoa il copione è stato quasi didattico. La squadra di D'Aversa ha avuto anche un buon approccio e le occasioni per colpire, ma al primo errore serio ha pagato. Al 26' Osmajic ha sfruttato la verticalizzazione di Traoré; al 38' un errore di da Candé ha permesso a Messias di servire nuovamente il montenegrino per lo 0-2. Due errori, due gol. Nove individuali in 12 giornate: nessuno ha fatto peggio.

Industry observers note that L'altra faccia della crisi è offensiva. Contro il Genoa Berardi ha avuto una grande occasione prima dell'intervallo, Laurienté ha costretto Bijlow a intervenire, ma il Sassuolo è rimasto ancora a zero. Il nuovo tecnico avrà bisogno di tempo per modificare principi, automatismi e mentalità ,a il calendario non aspetta. Domenica prossima arriverà il Napoli e il Sassuolo non vince dal 13 settembre, dal 3-2 contro la Juventus. Da allora sono arrivati un pareggio e sette sconfitte. La sensazione è che il lavoro necessario sia molto più profondo di un semplice cambio di allenatore. Con 31 gol subiti e una classifica ormai cortissima alle spalle, il tempo per trasformare i primi segnali in punti comincia già a pesare.

Speaking to SportMediaset on the sidelines of the Meet&Greet at the Milan Store in San Babila, via MilanNews, De Winter looked at the rise in his playing time, Amorim’s closeness to the group and much more.

In a recent development, you also took over at Reggio Emilia when Gabbia was unfortunately injured. You’re practically always there; what does that mean to you?

It has been revealed that “I’m playing a lot, it’s great to be playing. We’re playing a lot, and these days you train more on taking care of your body, keeping healthy, and right now I’m doing that more, but it’s great to be playing a lot of games. Playing a lot of games for Milan, and it’s even better to win games.”.

Sources indicate that it’s all great, but it wasn’t a given: you’ve earned this place as leader. Do you now feel like a leader of this AC Milan?

It has been revealed that “I feel good at this Milan club, and as I always say, I try to give what I can. It’s also true that I might have a more notable position this year. That might be true, but I always try to do my part, give my all, and help my teammates.”.

It’s clear, evident, that Amorim holds you in high regard, but what is Amorim like? An adjective.

“I’d say he’s very human. He’s one of us, he laughs, he has fun, but when he has to be serious, he’s serious. He lives with the group, the group feels close to him, and I think that gives the players a good feeling. It’s nice to work for him and with him.”.

Is it true that he got very angry after the defeat against Ferencvaros?

“Yes, but I think the whole group felt that we had played a very poor game, so, as I saw it, my teammates saw it too.”.

Are Ferencvaros and Bologna two games you’re ready to say “never again” to? Will Frosinone be a different team?

“Yes, exactly, as I said, we are very confident, but sometimes even too much so, and then all matches are difficult against whoever we play against, and we have to understand this swiftly and we can’t make the same mistakes.”.

Among the various critics, it’s said that this AC Milan team has enormous potential, but there are too many ups and downs. Does it need more consistency?

“Yes, I think it hurts even more when we lose because we know we can do well, we can win every game. So yes, when we really lose, in the locker room you feel like we’ve let ourselves down first and then everyone else.”.

Industry observers note that you recently became the father of a beautiful baby girl. What are your nights like as a dad?

“At night, I’m fine. My girlfriend is working really hard, so it’s a lot for me. I mean, I get up sometimes, but it’s much quieter. I think it’s harder for her.”.

And how much has life changed with the arrival of a daughter?

Industry observers note that “It’s changed a lot, I mean, I don’t know how to explain it. “I mean, crazy in a good way, yes. He likes to have fun, he likes to dance, he likes to talk, so he’s a bright spot, as they say, for the locker room, yes.”.

It has been revealed that “Well, that’s a good question. Yes, I miss her. I thought about it even when the little girl was born: I also want to score a goal, I mean, dedicate a goal to her, so I miss her, yes.”.

According to recent reports, “It’s become a routine now, so I always do the same things. You’re in the hotel, you take a shower, you play a little video game or you’re on your phone, so now I don’t even think about it, it’s really become a routine.”.

What does Maignan ask of you, defenders?

“He says to stay focused on the game because, as we know, one moment can change the game and at Milan it can also change a season, so it’s very crucial not to underestimate every moment and always stay focused.

It seems to me that there is a great understanding between you and Strahinja Pavlovic even off the pitch….

Industry observers note that “Yes, it’s true, he and I have a good relationship; we met last year. Then when you see him you might not think, I mean, I didn’t think he would be such a great friend, but we got along really well both on and off the pitch, it’s really nice to spend time with him.”.

Recent findings suggest that our 007s at Milanello tell us about some great ping pong matches between you and Pavlovic. Who’s the better player?

In a recent development, “This is difficult, but he started at a much higher level than me. But now I’ve improved a lot, although I have to say he’s even stronger. But yes, every day we start with a game of ping pong and then we start working.”.

According to recent reports, would you like your daughter to play soccer in the future? Are you planning a second child? Would you like to have a son who plays soccer?

“I want her to do what she wants, where she feels good, where she doesn’t feel pressured, and where she can express herself best. And then, going back to ping pong, I think there’s some video; maybe we can see me beat her.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leicester City’s rapid decline from the Premier League to League One means there has been a lot of change over the past two years. LCFC’s place as European football contenders is a thing of the past, and so are many of the players.

It has been revealed that among the mainstays in the Foxes’ Premier League days was right-back Ricardo Pereira, who joined from FC Porto in 2018 and grew into a starring role at the King Power Stadium. He was one of the league’s best in his position, but injuries hit and limited his involvement.

Pereira stayed throughout Leicester City’s yo-yo years, but when his contract came to an end earlier this year, it was decided that he would move on. And, over four months on from his release, he remains out of the game.

Pereira managed 39 appearances in Leicester City’s relegation season, proving he can still manage a demanding season despite previous injury challenges.

Sources indicate that his pedigree at the very top of the game with the Foxes and Porto has seen him grow into a leadership figure over the years. The experience he has to his name is of huge value to younger players and his character would swiftly see him become an influential figure in the dressing room.

Recent findings suggest that granted, the speed and physical traits Pereira revealed at his best aren’t as strong anymore. However, he has always been a technically gifted player in possession, and his pedigree helps him read the game well.

Sources indicate that pereira has shared images and videos of himself training during his time without a team. He would need time to get up to speed to play full games at a competitive level, but he has kept himself ticking over as he awaits his next opportunity after leaving LCFC.

It remains to be seen just what awaits Pereira after a long spell out of the game. Opportunities do dry up as the season moves on from the summer transfer window, so there might not be many intriguing options out there.

The MLS regular season has just ended, so the Leicester City man could join a team for their 2027 preparations to be ready to go for the new campaign. Alternatively though, Pereira may wish to see out the latter years of his career back in his home country of Portugal.

Teams in Liga Portugal would certainly benefit from his leadership and experience. Having broken through in his home country before leaving for bigger things, it could be a fitting end to his career to return and become an influential player for a top flight side.
